text: Feat 1 Dad Joke Single Action to Two Actions Auditory General Mental Skill Source Fools Aplenty Nethys Note: This is a part of the April Fool's content from Paizo's blogs. Using the power of punnery, you deliver a lovingly tailored joke at a creature within 60 feet. Attempt a skill check using the skill that would be used to identify the creature (e.g. Religion for a fiend); you can instead attempt a Lore check with a +2 circumstance bonus if the target is trained in that Lore or could be identified by that Lore when Recalling Knowledge. If you target a creature that isn’t a family member, this ability gains the incapacitation trait. The target is then immune to your Dad Jokes for 1 hour. If you spend two actions to use this ability by setting up an especially elaborate punchline, your target also takes 1d4 mental damage, plus 1d4 additional damage at 3rd level and every 2 levels thereafter, with a basic Will save against the higher of your class DC or spell DC. Critical Success The joke is so blindingly perfect-yet-awful that the target dissociates from reality. The creature is dazzled and stupefied 1 until the end of your next turn. Double the mental damage dealt to the target. Success The target is stupefied 1 until the end of your next turn or until the creature targets you with a hostile effect, whichever happens first. The target takes full mental damage. Failure The target is unaffected. Critical Failure The target is unaffected. Your allies who hear the joke are so embarrassed by it that they can’t treat you as an ally for any effects until the end of your next turn.

With a loud shout, you unleash your ki in a crackling shroud of thunder and lightning that engulfs your body. Until the end of your next turn, your unarmed attacks and weapons you wield that have the monk trait deal additional electricity damage equal to one-half your level and additional sonic damage equal to one-half your level.

 If you also know the [_ki blast_](/Spells.aspx?ID=484) ki spell, you can choose to deal either electricity or sonic damage with the spell instead of force while this effect is active (_ki blast_ loses the [force](/Traits.aspx?ID=610) trait and gains the [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586) or [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697) trait instead). Any creature who successfully [Grapples](/Actions.aspx?ID=2376) you or is successfully Grappled by you also takes this damage immediately after the Grapple check is resolved.

You [Leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=2298) toward an opponent. At any point in the Leap, you can make a single Strike against a creature within your reach. At 12th level, if you hit with this Strike, instead of finishing your Leap, you can immediately attempt a second Leap from the space where you struck the target of your Strike. You can make a single Strike against a target within your reach during this second Leap as well. At 16th level, you can attempt a third Leap if your second Strike hits, and you can attack a target at any point during this third Leap. All Leaps made during this activity gain a +10-foot status bonus to the total height or distance of your leap, and no two Strikes can target the same creature.

**Access**

</column>

---

You've started walking the path toward becoming a true Hellknight, though you're currently considered only an armiger. You've been taught how to terrorize others into compliance, but you also continually study the structure and hierarchy of [Hell](/Planes.aspx?ID=42). You must survive painful tests of your body and mind called reckonings that steady your willpower against all sorts of trauma. You gain resistance to mental damage equal to 1 + your number of archetype class feats from the Hellknight archetype. You become trained in [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40); if you were already trained, you become an expert instead. 

In addition, you gain the [Additional Lore](/Feats.aspx?ID=5114) general feat for Hell Lore; if you were already trained in Hell Lore, you also become trained in a [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) skill of your choice.

<title level="2">Hellknight Dedication leads to...</title>
[Advanced Order Training](/Feats.aspx?ID=8827), [Ardent Armiger](/Feats.aspx?ID=8813), [Armiger's Protection](/Feats.aspx?ID=8814), [Diabolic Certitude](/Feats.aspx?ID=8815), [Hellknight Mobility](/Feats.aspx?ID=8820), [Hellknight Preferment](/Feats.aspx?ID=8818), [Hellknight Signifer Preferment](/Feats.aspx?ID=8819), [Hellknight-Errant](/Feats.aspx?ID=8817), [Mortification](/Feats.aspx?ID=8816), [Order Cross-Training](/Feats.aspx?ID=8830), [Order Training](/Feats.aspx?ID=8822), [Sense Iniquity](/Feats.aspx?ID=8823)

</column>

---

You've trained to resist the manipulations of [fiends](/Traits.aspx?ID=600), and your Hellknight discipline makes you difficult to influence. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saves against effects that could inflict the [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=64) or [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) conditions.

 If a [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effect would compel you to act in a way that violates your Hellknight order's tenets (as determined by the GM), you can attempt to break free from the effect as a free action triggered by receiving the violating order, and you gain a new Will save against the effect. You can attempt this save even if the effect would normally prevent you from acting of your own volition. You can attempt this new save only once for a given effect, even if you're compelled to violate your order's tenets multiple times. You can't receive a worse result on this Will save than you originally got against the compelling mental effect.
name: Ardent Armiger

If you were already trained in light armor and medium armor, you gain training in [Hellknight half plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=24) and [Hellknight plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=25). Whenever you gain a class feature that grants you expert or greater proficiency in any type of armor (but not unarmored defense), you also gain that proficiency in the armor types granted to you by this feat.  In addition, when you choose this feat, you receive a non-magical suit of Hellknight armor of a type you become trained in (Hellknight breastplate, Hellknight half plate, or Hellknight plate).

Either through unfortunate circumstances or your own choice, you remain a Hellknight armiger instead of entering the true ranks of your order, though you still believe in the tenets of law and order. You likely take on an adventuring life with a group of like-minded individuals who aren't Hellknights. The resistance to mental damage you gained from the Hellknight Dedication feat increases to 5 + your number of archetype class feats from the Hellknight archetype.

 You also gain the Warding Shift action, which allows you to keep your allies from harm.

 **Warding Shift** <actions string="Single Action" /> **Requirements** You're adjacent to a willing ally; **Effect** You move the adjacent willing ally 5 feet in any direction and can Step into the space the ally vacated.

**Special** You can't take both this feat and [Hellknight Preferment](/Feats.aspx?ID=8818) or [Hellknight Signifer Preferment](/Feats.aspx?ID=8819).

</column>

---

You've bolstered your force of will with the power of the Measure and the Chain. You've officially joined the ranks of Hellknight signifers, and you receive a signifer's mask, often devoid of eyeholes or other decorative features. The mask doesn't obscure your vision, though it makes it impossible for others to see your eyes. While wearing your signifer's mask, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) checks to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=2389), [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) checks to [Coerce](/Actions.aspx?ID=2394), and Deception DCs against [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=2302). You gain expert proficiency rank in [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) (or in another skill in which you're trained of your choice, if you were already an expert in Intimidation), as well as in your choice of [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43), [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44), or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46).

**Special** You can't take both this feat and [Hellknight-Errant](/Feats.aspx?ID=8817) or [Hellknight Preferment](/Feats.aspx?ID=8818).

<title level="2">Hellknight Signifer Preferment leads to...</title>

The flames of your magic mark a target as an enemy of order. If your next action is to Cast a non-cantrip Spell that deals fire damage, that spell brands the target with a mark only you can see if it fails its saving throw. This brand lasts for 1 week. For as long as the target is branded, you always know the general direction and approximate distance of the target's current location, as long as it's on the same plane. You also know the direction the branded target is currently moving, if any, as well as any conditions affecting it. You can have only one brand active at a time.

<title

    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Steel Falcon Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8848) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=572" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 34

**Archetype** [Steel Falcon](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=374)

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39)

**Access**
You're invited by a current member of the Eagle Knights or the People's Council.

</column>

---

You serve as an envoy of the ideals of Andoran, whether it's in a foreign court or on the field of battle. Your training in the Steel Falcons enables you to anticipate the attitudes of others to achieve your goals. You gain the Size Up action.

 **Size Up** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) You designate a single, non-[mindless](/Traits.aspx?ID=652) creature as your focus and assess its motivations. You must be able to see and hear the creature. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks when you [Sense the Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=2302) of your focus and a +2 circumstance bonus to your Perception DC should your focus attempt to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=2389) or [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=2390) against you. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38), [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39), and [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) checks against your focus. You can only have one creature designated as your focus at a time. If you use Size Up against a creature when you already have a creature designated, the prior creature loses the designation and the new focus gains the designation. Your designation otherwise lasts until your next daily preparations.

**Special** You can take this dedication even if you haven't taken more than two non-dedication feats from the [Eagle Knight](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=314) archetype.

<title level="2">Steel Falcon Dedication leads to...</title>
[Denounce Tyranny](/Feats.aspx?ID=8849), [Frightening Indignation](/Feats.aspx?ID=8857), [Gray Corsair Training](/Feats.aspx?ID=8850), [Liberty's Promise](/Feats.aspx?ID=8851), [Perplex](/Feats.aspx?ID=8856), [Uncanny Prediction](/Feats.aspx?ID=8853)
name: Steel Falcon Dedication

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Auditory" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=541" />
<trait label="Linguistic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=642" />

<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=647" />

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 35

**Archetype** [Steel Falcon](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=374)

**Prerequisites**
[Steel Falcon Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8848)

**Requirements**
You witnessed a creature harm an ally, harm a noncombatant, or commit a wantonly evil act in the last round.

</column>

---

You call out a creature's despicable or cowardly actions, disrupting its alliances or even making its allies ashamed to be seen with it. Attempt a [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) check and compare the result to the Will DCs of up to three of the triggering creature's allies within 30 feet of you. If you succeed on the check, the target refuses to treat the triggering creature as an ally for 1 round (2 rounds on a critical success). It's possible to get a different degree of success for each target. If you're a master in Diplomacy, you can instead target up to five creatures, and if you're legendary in Diplomacy, you can target up to 10 creatures.

[Grave Sense](/Feats.aspx?ID=885) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [World Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=6) pg. 47

**Archetype** [Lastwall Sentry](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=15)

**Prerequisites**
[Lastwall Sentry Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=882)

</column>

---

Your time spent hunting the undead allows you to sense them. You sense undead as a [vague sense](/Rules.aspx?ID=413) similar to a human’s sense of smell, an uncomfortable sensation akin to smelling something cloying and rotting. When in proximity to the undead, you eventually sense their presence, though you might not do so instantly, and you can’t pinpoint their location. An undead using a disguise or otherwise trying to hide its presence must attempt a [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) check against your Perception DC to hide its presence from you. If the creature succeeds at its Deception check, it is then temporarily immune to your Grave Sense for 1 day.

Few would even suspect that you're a member of the Eagle Knights, and you use the tricks of the spymaster's trade to keep it that way. If you were already trained in Espionage Lore, you also become trained in a [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) skill of your choice. 

During your daily preparations, you can brush up on a specific field to gain the trained proficiency rank in one Lore skill of your choice. This proficiency lasts until you prepare again. Since this proficiency is temporary, you can't use it as a prerequisite for a skill increase or a permanent character option like a feat. If you have master proficiency in Espionage Lore, you gain expert proficiency in the chosen skill instead, and if you have legendary proficiency in Espionage Lore, you gain master proficiency in the skill.

If you've taken a [hostile action](/Rules.aspx?ID=300) against it this round, your result can be no better than a failure. **Critical Success** You and the target are considered allies until the end of your next turn or until you take a hostile action against it, whichever comes first. **Success** As critical success, but lasts until the end of your turn or until you take a hostile action against it, whichever comes first.
**Failure** No effect.
**Critical Failure** The target knows you attempted to fool it and plays along. You're [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) to the target until the beginning of your next turn.
name: Feign Innocence

You use your shield to protect your allies, not just yourself, especially against the undead. ---

You expect the same level of urbane sophistication from your allies as you possess, so whenever one of them succumbs to egregious behavior from a mental effect, you're immediately mortified. How dare they make you look bad! Whether you respond with noisy contempt or quiet distress, your reaction gives your ally a second chance to shake off the effect and save the moment, at least socially. Your ally rerolls the triggering Will saving throw with a +1 circumstance bonus and uses the higher result. Regardless of the result of the save, your ally is temporarily immune to Such a Disgrace! for 10 minutes.

once per day

**Prerequisites**
[Dandy Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6302)

**Trigger**
You’re about to roll initiative.

</column>

---

In socially exclusive venues like the Ivy District's Bloom Cabaret, you've learned how to make an entrance. This confidence doesn't betray you when you find yourself about to enter combat, allowing you to throw enemies temporarily off-balance. Once per day, you can choose to not roll initiative. Instead, you voluntarily go last. If more than one character uses this ability or another ability to go last, use the normal rules for resolving a tie: NPCs and monsters act before PCs, and within those groups, the creature can choose whichever order they want.

 Enemies who can see you must attempt a Will saving throw against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. On a failure, the enemy is overcome with anticipation for what you'll do or say next and can't use reactions for 1 round.

 In addition, during your first turn, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to the first Deception, Diplomacy, or Intimidation check you attempt.
name: Bloom Cabaret Entrance

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

**Prerequisites**

</column>

---

Gods need followers, and you know that its best to gather a flock in the present to support you in your endeavor. Of course, you'll reward their faith in you in the future when you become a true deity. You can spend 1 week of downtime in a settlement to evangelize your coming godhood and establish a small group of disciples to your faith. Once this group has been established, these disciples are always helpful to you. You can use Religion to [Request](/Actions.aspx?ID=2393) something of them, though your request must be able to be performed by the type of people who would follow you, at the GM's discretion. If you critically succeed at this check, your disciples give a piece of helpful advice or let you in on a small secret, granting you or a member of your party a +2 circumstance bonus to the first skill check you attempt when acting on the favor. If you critically fail this check, your disciples' attitude toward you doesn't worsen.

 You can have three groups of disciples at any one time (or five if you're legendary in Religion). If you exceed this number, the oldest group disbands and must be established again if you return to that settlement.
name: Gather Disciples
prerequisite: Starstone Aspirant Dedication; Master in Religion

You recover an additional 5 Hit Points from a successful attempt to Treat your Wounds or use Battle Medicine on you. After you or an ally use Battle Medicine on you, you become temporarily immune to that Battle Medicine for only 1 hour, instead of 1 day.

[Ka Stone Ritual](/Feats.aspx?ID=889) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [World Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=6) pg. 59

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) The Prerequisites entry for Ka Stone Ritual is “Living Monolith Dedication” rather than “Living Monolith Dedication, a sphinx or living monolith with this feat performs a ritual with you”. Characters with the Living Monolith Dedication feat have access to Ka Stone Ritual_

**Archetype** [Living Monolith](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=16)

**Prerequisites**
[Living Monolith Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=888); a [sphinx](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=209) or living monolith with this feat performs a ritual with you

</column>

---

You inscribe your true name on your _ka stone_, as well as oaths to gods and pharaohs, and embed it in your forehead in a special ritual with a sphinx or with a living monolith who already has this feat. The _ka stone_ is an invested magic item that you automatically invest each day. It can’t be removed without your permission, nor can it be dispelled, and you can never lose investiture in the ka stone. Its Bulk is negligible.

 The ka stone grants you a +1 item bonus to saves against death effects and negative effects, which increases to +2 at 8th level, +3 at 14th level, and +4 at 20th level.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> (envision), or a different activation if otherwise specified;  **Frequency** a number of times each day equal to the number of class feats you have from the Living Monolith archetype;   **Effect** You cast [_enlarge_](/Spells.aspx?ID=102) on yourself or use one of the other activated abilities granted by a later Living Monolith feat.

<title level="2">Ka Stone Ritual leads to...</title>
[Attunement to Stone](/Feats.aspx?ID=892), [Fortified Flesh](/Feats.aspx?ID=891), [Judgment of the Monolith](/Feats.aspx?ID=893), [Stone Blood](/Feats.aspx?ID=890), [Stone Communion](/Feats.aspx?ID=894)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 7"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Paragon Battle Medicine](/Feats.aspx?ID=8890) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=615" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=695" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 60

**Archetype** [Pure Legion Enforcer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=377) (Level 7)

**Prerequisites**
[Battle Medicine](/Feats.aspx?ID=5125); Master in [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=42)

**Access**
You’re from Rahadoum.

</column>

---

You've learned the modern uses of Battle Medicine originated by Kassi Aziril. When you successfully use Battle Medicine, you can also reduce the target's [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91), [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71), or [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61) condition by 1 (this has no effect if you are subject to an effect continually applying the clumsy condition, like enlarge). If you are legendary in Medicine, you can choose to reduce the target's [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) or [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93) condition by 1 instead, and if you have the [Godless Healing](/Feats.aspx?ID=8888) feat, you can choose to reduce the target's [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) or [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) condition by 1 instead. If you have the [Mortal Healing](/Feats.aspx?ID=8889) feat, you can reduce all available conditions by 1 for a target who hasn't benefited from [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509) or [healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623) magic in the last 24 hours, and if you roll a critical success before applying the effects of the feat, you reduce all available conditions by 2 for that target instead.
name: Paragon Battle Medicine

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 60 **Archetype** [Pure Legion Enforcer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=377) **Prerequisites** member of the Pure Legion --- You are sworn to uphold the Laws of Mortality within the borders of Rahadoum. As part of your commissioning, you learned about the different types of worship and divine magic that you might encounter. You become trained in Intimidation and Religion. If you are already trained in one or both of these skills, you become an expert in that skill. If you are already an expert in both skills, you become trained in a skill of your choice. You also gain the Recognize Spell skill feat. Whenever you attempt to recognize a divine spell, you always learn it is divine and gain a +2 circumstance bonus to the Religion skill check. Finally, you gain the following edicts and anathema. Knowingly committing acts that violate the anathema result in you losing access to abilities granted by this archetype, as determined by your GM. You can regain these lost abilities by spending an appropriate amount of time rededicating yourself to the Pure Legion, typically by donating an amount equal to 20 gp × your level to appropriate causes and eschewing all divine magic (including spells cast by others) for at least 1 day. **Edicts** confiscate, contain, or destroy all divine objects in Rahadoum; drive out divine casters from Rahadoum
**Anathema** use divine abilities, items, or spells; permit proselytizing of religion in Rahadoum; worship a deity Pure Legion Enforcer Dedication leads to... [Edict of Mortality](/Feats.aspx?ID=8892), [Mortal Possibility](/Feats.aspx?ID=8900), [No Gods, Only Mortals!](/Feats.aspx?ID=8894), [Repelling Enforcer](/Feats.aspx?ID=8899), [Shake Off the Gods](/Feats.aspx?ID=8896), [Throttle the Divine](/Feats.aspx?ID=8897), [Traces of the Divine](/Feats.aspx?ID=8895), [Unassailable Enforcer](/Feats.aspx?ID=8893), [Wrath Against the Divine](/Feats.aspx?ID=8898)
name: Pure Legion Enforcer Dedication

</column>

---

Using clever gnomish engineering, you can quickly erect small barriers in which your snares are hidden. When you prepare snares for quick deployment, you can prepare some of them as barricade snares. A barricade snare consists of a small barricade in which the snare is hidden, but it costs two of your quick deployment snares. Though creatures can automatically see the barricade, the snare hidden inside the barricade must be detected like a standard snare, but with a +2 circumstance bonus to the DC. The barricade occupies the same space as the snare and is 5 feet high; it provides standard cover, can be Climbed with a successful DC 12 Athletics check, has an AC of 10, Hardness 5, and 20 Hit Points, and is immune to critical hits and precision damage. The barricade lasts as long as the snare does. A creature triggers and is affected by the hidden snare when it attempts to [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=2374) the barricade or successfully attacks the barricade while adjacent to it. The snare and barricade are destroyed when the snare is triggered or if the barricade is destroyed, whichever comes first.

**Special** Even if you have the Surprise Snare feat, you must craft a barricade snare in an empty square.
name: Barricade Snare

>
[Rose Warden Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8906) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=572" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 84

**Archetype** [Rose Warden](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=378)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48); you worship [Milani](/Deities.aspx?ID=352)

</column>

---

As a follower of the Everbloom, you stand up against tyranny and oppression, understanding that revolution against an unjust ruler must sometimes be enacted in secret. You become trained in Deception. If you're already trained in Deception, you become an expert in your choice of Deception or Stealth. When you get a critical success to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=2389) to a figure of authority, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your Fortitude DC and saving throws against being [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63), [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=64), [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77), [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81), or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90) by that figure of authority for 24 hours.

 You add the edicts and anathema of Milani to your own (see sidebar). Failing to uphold edicts or committing acts that violate the anathema result in you losing access to any abilities granted by this archetype, as determined by your GM. You can regain these lost abilities through the atone ritual as normal.

<title level="2">Rose Warden Dedication leads to...</title>
[Blessed Thorn Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=8907), [Holy Bloom](/Feats.aspx?ID=8908), [Liberated Mind](/Feats.aspx?ID=8911), [Rise Up!](/Feats.aspx?ID=8914), [Unbalancing Appearance](/Feats.aspx?ID=8909), [Unfettering Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=8910), [Wall of Roses](/Feats.aspx?ID=8912)
name: Rose Warden Dedication
prerequisite: Trained in Stealth; you worship Milani

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Archetype** [Rose Warden](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=378)

**Prerequisites**
[Rose Warden Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8906)

</column>

---

Though you might not be a priest of Milani, her divine spirit flows through you. You gain holy sanctification. Select the [freedom](/Domains.aspx?ID=77) or [zeal](/Domains.aspx?ID=100) domain. You gain the initial domain spell for that domain. If you don't have one, you gain a focus pool of 1 Focus Point. You can [Refocus](/Actions.aspx?ID=2621) by praying to Milani or by working with others to plan a just uprising. You become trained in spell attack modifier and spell DC, and your spellcasting attribute for these spells is Wisdom.

**Special** You can choose this feat a second time, gaining the initial domain spell of the domain you didn't gain the first time.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />

---

Roses are the symbol of Milani, and you can call forth a wall of them to stymie those who don't follow her teachings. You can cast [_wall of thorns_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1752) once per day as a 4th-rank divine innate spell. The wall is immune to fire and the piercing damage its thorns deal counts as silver for the purposes of resistances. Followers of Milani don't treat the wall's spaces as difficult terrain and don't take damage when they enter one of the wall's spaces.
name: Wall of Roses

You tense your muscles to make yourself neutrally buoyant and more difficult to move. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your Fortitude or Reflex DC against attempts to [Reposition](/Actions.aspx?ID=2379) or [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=2380) you. This bonus also applies to saving throws against spells or effects that attempt to force you to move. If any effect would force you to move 10 feet or more, attempt a DC 11 flat check. On a success, you move only 5 feet. Additionally, you don't have to take a [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=2381) action each turn to avoid sinking or moving with the current.

**Access**
You're from Isger or a member of the Sisterhood of the Golden Erinys.

</column>

---

The fighting style of the Sisterhood of the Golden Erinys is rooted in their understanding of devils. You gain the [Additional Lore](/Feats.aspx?ID=5114) general feat for Devil Lore. When you choose this feat, you can choose to become sanctified as unholy. You gain access to the asp coil. You have familiarity with the [asp coil](/Weapons.aspx?ID=233) and [scourge](/Weapons.aspx?ID=531), treating them as simple weapons for the purposes of proficiency. If you're unholy, your Strikes using those weapons and your unarmed Strikes gain the [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521) trait.

Whether you're a keen student of vengeance or you picked up techniques after being a common target for the sisters' punishment, you've learned to dig painfully into your opponent's flesh. In this stance, you can make fury's fang unarmed attacks. These deal 1d6 piercing damage; are in the [brawling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4) group; and have the [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=526), [backstabber](/Traits.aspx?ID=544), [finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=602), [forceful](/Traits.aspx?ID=611), [nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=661), and [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=719) traits.

 While in the stance, if you critically hit with a melee Strike that deals piercing damage, the target is [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) 1 (with a DC to remove equal to your class DC); this is in addition to any critical specialization effect you might gain from the attack.

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 120 **Archetype** [Nidalese Horselord](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=381) **Prerequisites** Trained in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43); [horse](/Companions.aspx?ID=76) animal companion **Access** You’re from Nidal. --- Thanks to the deep bond you share with your Nidalese horse, the two of you gain remarkable abilities. You both gain darkvision and a +1 status bonus to saving throws against effects with the [darkness](/Traits.aspx?ID=569) or [shadow](/Traits.aspx?ID=693) trait. Your horse's Speed also increases by 5 feet. You gain the following edicts and anathema. **Edicts** oppose the forces of the Umbral Court where possible, provide comfort to those who suffer in darkness
**Anathema** mistreat your horse, worship Zon-Kuthon or permanently ally with those who worship Zon-Kuthon **Special** You can pledge yourself to the cause of the Nidalese horselords if you've already taken the [Cavalier Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6286) feat, allowing you to take this dedication feat even if you haven't taken two additional cavalier feats. Nidalese Horselord Dedication leads to... [Defy Chains](/Feats.aspx?ID=8946), [Dismounting Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=8942), [Face Your Fears](/Feats.aspx?ID=8938), [Fear No Pain!](/Feats.aspx?ID=8940), [Gallop Across Shadow](/Feats.aspx?ID=8947), [Horselord's Bond](/Feats.aspx?ID=8944), [Repel Darkness](/Feats.aspx?ID=8939), [Shadowpiercing Charge](/Feats.aspx?ID=8945), [Swallow Pain](/Feats.aspx?ID=8943), [Swift Support](/Feats.aspx?ID=8941)
name: Nidalese Horselord Dedication
prerequisite: Trained in Nature; horse animal companion

A lifetime of facing Nidal's terrors has taught you to fight through fear. Although you aren't immune to it, you can subdue the emotion to such an extent that many believe it doesn't affect you. Your stoicism and courage seem to drive off darkness and shadow. For 1 minute, you suppress magical [darkness](/Traits.aspx?ID=569) effects of a rank equal to or lower than half your level rounded up within a 10-foot emanation. This doesn't provide light, but merely restores the area to its natural illumination level. You can Dismiss this aura.

 If your horse is at least a mature animal companion, you can use Repel Darkness to cause the aura to emanate from your horse instead of you, as long as your horse is within 100 feet.
name: Repel Darkness

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 121

**Prerequisites**
[Nidalese Horselord Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8937)

**Requirements**
You are mounted on your horse, and your last action was to [Command an Animal](/Actions.aspx?ID=2400) to order your horse to Stride at least once.

</column>

---

You leap from your horse, using the momentum of its movement to deal a devastating blow with your melee weapon. You use the [Mount](/Actions.aspx?ID=2314) action to dismount your horse but can move to any space within 10 feet of your mount, as long as your horse moved at least 15 feet. You then make a melee Strike. This counts as two attacks when calculating your multiple attack penalty. If this Strike hits, you deal an extra die of weapon damage. If you're at least 14th level, increase this to two extra dice.
name: Dismounting Strike

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=662" />
<trait label="Sanctified" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=519" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 121

**Archetype** [Nidalese Horselord](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=381)

**Prerequisites**
[Nidalese Horselord Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8937)

**Trigger**
A fiend within 15 feet of you damages you with a Strike.

</column>

---

You turn to face a fiend that attacked you, looking them squarely in the eyes (if it has them) and showing no fear. You increase the amount of damage you take by 4d6, and deal 4d6 spirit damage to the triggering fiend. The damage you take and deal increases to 5d6 at 18th level.

 In addition, if the fiend has an aura and you're in it, you can attempt an Intimidation check to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) the aura's effect, using half your level rounded up as the counteract rank. If you succeed, the effects of the aura are suppressed until the end of the triggering fiend's next turn.
name: Defy Chains

</title>

<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=662" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 121

[Nidalese Horselord Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8937)

</column>

---

Though your enemy wields shadow and darkness as weapons, they are no impediment to you when you ride your trusted horse. To that end, your mount can step onto patches of darkness as if they were solid. When your horse moves through an area of [darkness](/Traits.aspx?ID=569), it can treat empty spaces as solid ground. This allows your horse to move across gaps bridged by darkness or even into the air, ascending or descending at a maximum of a 45-degree angle. If your horse isn't on actual solid ground and the area your horse is in becomes [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2401) or brighter, your horse falls.

[Basic Red Mantis Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=896) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [World Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=6) pg. 71

**Archetype** [Red Mantis Assassin](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=17)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13); [Red Mantis Assassin Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=895)

</column>

---

You have learned limited divine magic from your Red Mantis training. You gain the [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=72) activity. You’re a prepared spellcaster, able to prepare two cantrips and one 1st-level spell each day. You prepare these spells from a Red Mantis assassin spellbook, similar to a wizard’s, containing three cantrips and two 1st-level spells. All the spells in your Red Mantis assassin spellbook, from this and later feats, must be either transmutation or illusion spells from the arcane spell list or a spell from the following list: [_clairaudience_](/Spells.aspx?ID=39), [_clairvoyance_](/Spells.aspx?ID=40), [_darkness_](/Spells.aspx?ID=59), [_dimension door_](/Spells.aspx?ID=69), [_modify memory_](/Spells.aspx?ID=200), [_obscuring mist_](/Spells.aspx?ID=210), [_paralyze_](/Spells.aspx?ID=213), [_see invisibility_](/Spells.aspx?ID=271), [_true strike_](/Spells.aspx?ID=345). Regardless of their usual magical tradition, your Red Mantis assassin spells are divine spells, as are any Red Mantis focus spells you gain.

 You can prepare two cantrips and one 1st-level spell each day from those found in your Red Mantis assassin spellbook. You’re trained in spell attack rolls and spell DCs for casting divine spells. Your key spellcasting ability for these spells is Charisma.

<title level="2">Basic Red Mantis Magic leads to...</title>
[Achaekek's Grip](/Feats.aspx?ID=2162), [Advanced Red Mantis Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=897), [Mantis Form](/Feats.aspx?ID=899)
name: Basic Red Mantis Magic
prerequisite: Trained in Religion; Red Mantis Assassin Dedication

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=615" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=695" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=320) pg. 159

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) The Quick Setup feat is not permitted in Pathfinder Society play._

**Prerequisites**
Master in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4)

</column>

---

You have learned to setup simple crafting jobs with ease. Your setup time for consumables that are at least 6 levels lower than you is 1 day, and your setup time for permanent items 6 levels lower than you is 3 days.

If you rush the setup and reduce the setup time for consumables at least 6 levels lower than you to less than 1 day, you can instead set them up in just 2 hours (allowing you to do so during an adventuring day if you have access to your tools and materials). If you rush the setup of a permanent item at least 6 levels lower than you and reduce the setup time to less than 1 day, you can perform the setup in 4 hours.
name: Quick Setup

**Source** [Pathfinder #223: Hell's Destiny](/Sources.aspx?ID=336) pg. 223 **Archetype** [Chelaxian Scion](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=384) **Prerequisites** [Chelaxian Scion Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8971) --- Through consistent (and often punishing) practice, you’ve learned how to use your house’s preferred weapons. You have familiarity with either one martial weapon of your choice; two simple or martial weapons of your choice from your house’s preferred weapons list; or one advanced weapon of your choice from your house’s preferred weapons list. For the purpose of proficiency, treat any of these selections that are martial weapons as simple weapons and any that are advanced weapons as martial weapons. If you’re at least an expert in one of the selected weapons, you get the critical specialization effect of that weapon when you get a critical hit with it. **Charthagnion**: Weapons with the [disarm](/Traits.aspx?ID=577) or [parry](/Traits.aspx?ID=667) trait
**Elliendo**: [Brawling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4) weapons and [knives](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=9)
**Henderthane**: [Hammers](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=8) and [picks](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=10)
**Jeggare**: One-handed [swords](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=15)
**Leroung**: [Clubs](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=5) and [shields](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=12)
**Narikopolus**: [Bows](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=3)
**Sarini**: [Flails](/Weapons.aspx?ID=374)
**Thrune**: [Clubs](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=5) and [crossbows](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=17) In addition, you gain the For My House! action. **For My House!** **Frequency** once per minute; **Effect** You announce your house affiliation, either by declaring it aloud (giving this ability the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541) trait) or openly displaying your house heraldry (giving this ability the [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727) trait). Until the beginning of your next turn, your weapon Strikes and spells deal an additional 1 damage to any creature that witnessed the display. If you’re an expert in [Cheliax Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41), Genealogy Lore, Heraldry Lore, [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45), or Warfare Lore, the additional damage increases to 2. The damage increases to 3 if you’re a master in the skill or 4 if you’re legendary in the skill.
name: Aristocratic Arms

[Patronize the Arts](/Feats.aspx?ID=8975) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #223: Hell's Destiny](/Sources.aspx?ID=336) pg. 223

**Archetype** [Chelaxian Scion](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=384)

**Prerequisites**
[Chelaxian Scion Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8971)

**Trigger**
An ally within 30 feet of you critically succeeds at an attack roll or skill check.

</column>

---

A true aristocrat knows how to encourage their best hirelings, ensuring loyalty and future excellence. You praise the triggering ally, granting them one of the following benefits. The ally is then immune to this ability for 1 day. 

**Eagerness:** Invigorated by praise, the ally can [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=1434), [Interact](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297) with a nearby object, [Leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=2298), [Reload](/Rules.aspx?ID=2196), or [Step](/Actions.aspx?ID=2304) as a reaction. 

**Persistence:** For 1 minute, the ally gains [temporary Hit Points](/Rules.aspx?ID=2321) equal to half your level plus your Charisma modifier. 

**Validation:** If the ally has the [panache class feature](/Classes.aspx?ID=63), they gain panache.
name: Patronize the Arts

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #223: Hell's Destiny](/Sources.aspx?ID=336) pg. 223

**Archetype** [Chelaxian Scion](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=384)

**Frequency**
once per minute

**Prerequisites**
[Chelaxian Scion Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8971); Trained in [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40); expert in Will

**Trigger**
You’re targeted by an [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590) effect or effect that would give you the [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=64) condition.

</column>

---

Like the [archdevil](/DeityCategories.aspx?ID=4) [Dispater](/Deities.aspx?ID=397), you maintain an unshakable poise even under impossible stress. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to the triggering saving throw or to your Will DC against the triggering effect. If you critically succeed at the saving throw (or if the source of the effect critically fails its skill check, such as to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=2395) you), you gain [temporary Hit Points](/Rules.aspx?ID=2321) equal to half your level until the end of the effect’s source’s next turn. If the effect originated from a creature, you can Demoralize that creature once as a free action on your next turn; if the creature was temporarily immune to your attempts to Demoralize it, it loses that immunity.
name: Stoic as Hell

The target then attempts a Fortitude save against your class DC. **Critical Success** The sigil immediately vanishes, and the creature is unaffected.
**Success** The sigil acts as a magnet for your fiery attacks, granting the creature a –1 penalty to its saves and AC against your fire impulses. The sigil lasts until the end of your next turn or until the creature spends at least 1 action obeying your command, whichever happens first.
**Failure** At the start of the creature’s next turn, if it doesn’t use their first action to obey the command, the sigil ignites as it vanishes, dealing 8d6 fire damage and 2d6 [persistent fire damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) to the creature.
**Critical Failure** The creature must spend the first action of its next turn to obey your command; it can’t [Delay](/Actions.aspx?ID=2294). The sigil vanishes at the end of its turn; it ignites if the creature didn’t use all its remaining actions to continue to obey your command, dealing 8d6 fire damage and 2d6 persistent fire damage to the creature. --- **Level (+2)** The damage increases by 1d6, and the persistent damage increases by 1d6.

You’re immune to the effects of your own Drowning Mist. Critical Success The creature is unaffected and becomes temporarily immune to the effects of this impulse for 24 hours. Success The creature is unaffected. Failure Moisture seeps into the creature’s lungs, making the creature sickened 1. Critical Failure As failure, but sickened 2.

You sprout wings with steel feathers, resembling those of the [celestial](/Traits.aspx?ID=551) [Talmandor](/NPCs.aspx?ID=4835). With a powerful flap, the wings propel you across the battlefield, slicing foes and restraints along your path. Until the end of your turn, you gain a [fly Speed](/Rules.aspx?ID=2350) equal to your land Speed or 40 feet, whichever is greater. You then [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312) up to your Speed, and this movement doesn't trigger reactions.

Choose one foe and one ally you're adjacent to at any point during this movement. Using one wing's sharpened edge, you can use a 1-action [Elemental Blast](/Actions.aspx?ID=2125) as a melee Strike using the metal element against the foe. With the other wing, you can help the ally break free of an effect [grabbing](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77), [restraining](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90), [immobilizing](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81), or [paralyzing](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85) them; they either attempt a new save against one such effect that allows a save, or they attempt to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) as a free action. You tinker, create, and repair gear as you adventure. You can spend part of your daily preparations adjusting your group’s equipment. This allows you to attempt to [Repair](/Actions.aspx?ID=2384) up to five items during that time.

You gain access to a new exploration activity: Tinker on the Go. So long as you have two free hands and have access to the necessary tools, you can make Crafting progress while out traveling. At the GM’s discretion, you might not be able to Tinker on the Go for projects that require extensive infrastructure, such as a smithing forge. Otherwise, time spent exploring can count toward a day of crafting progress, as long as 8 hours of time get used in this way. 

If you lead a [troop](/Rules.aspx?ID=3439), you maintain their equipment in addition to your companions’ gear. Once per day when you Command the troop in a skirmish encounter, you can increase the DC of their offensive actions by 1 until the beginning of your next turn.

Master in [Games Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41)

</column>

---

You’re a master of strategy games, able to translate strategies and mechanics from these games to the actual battles they were created to simulate. You can use your proficiency rank in [Games Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) for anything that requires proficiency in Warfare Lore (such as prerequisites) and use your Games Lore modifier in place of your Warfare Lore modifier for checks. You can use Games Lore to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=2392) on military professionals, such as mercenaries and commanders. Your reputation as a strategist opens up opportunities while you’re in a military camp, near a battlefield, or somewhere else that has numerous non‑hostile soldiers, allowing you to [Earn Income](/Actions.aspx?ID=2364) with Games Lore with a task level of at least your level – 1. 

If you [lead a troop](/Rules.aspx?ID=3439) and have had time to create a [skirmish bond](/Rules.aspx?ID=3452) with them, you’ve also spent time going over the finer points of strategy and even played against many members of your troop. Once per day, you can roll Games Lore for initiative when leading this troop.
name: As on the Board, so on the Battlefield

May contain spoilers from Hell's Destiny **Source** [Pathfinder #223: Hell's Destiny](/Sources.aspx?ID=336) pg. 231 **Prerequisites** Master in [Warfare Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) --- You’re a wild card on the battlefield, inventing unpredictable tactics and surprising foes. You employ one of these strategies, adding either your choice of the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541) or [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727) trait. Attempt a [Warfare Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) check against the [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=2040) DC of a creature within 30 feet, after which the target becomes temporarily immune to further uses of Improvise Strategy for 1 hour. **Special** Once per day, if you lead a troop that has a [skirmish bond](/Rules.aspx?ID=3452), you can Improvise Strategy to attempt a Warfare Lore check against a standard DC for your troop’s level, rather than targeting a foe. If you succeed, your troop replaces its current skirmish bond with another of your choice until the end of your next turn. **Critical Success** The target gains one of the following conditions of your choice until the end of your next turn: [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61) 1, [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65), [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58), or [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 1. The target can end the effect by using either a single action with the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) trait to regain their bearings (if your strategy had the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541) trait) or an [Interact](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297) action to rub their eyes (if your strategy had the [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727) trait). In addition, the target isn’t temporarily immune to further uses of Improvise Strategy.
**Success** As critical success, but the target is temporarily immune to further uses of Improvise Strategy.
**Failure** The target is unaffected.
**Critical Failure** The target sees through the gambit, leaving you [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) until the beginning of your next turn.

If the creature is already in the water, on a success, in addition the normal effects of Grapple, you drag the creature 10 feet deeper into the water, moving 10 feet with the creature. Moving a creature into water or deeper into water using Steal for the Depths is forced movement for the creature but not for you.

When you use Plot the Future, you can instead contemplate a person that you’ve gotten to observe within 30 feet for at least 1 minute. You deduce places they will habitually be in the next week and what time of day they’ll be there. For each location, you deduce the likelihood that they will be two of the following: alone, unarmed, or unaware. You also gain a piece of advice for each location suggesting a course of action you or your allies could take that might make it more or less likely for them to be in the chosen states. The GM determines the locations the person will visit and when, as well as the likelihood they’ll be alone, unarmed, or unaware.

Spend enough time in Hell Harbor, and you pick up the paranoia encouraged by Arronax Endymion. Maybe you served under him on the _Tyrannous_, escaped his executioners, or had a friend who wasn’t so lucky; whatever the reason, you have some of his wariness. Unless you’re a willing target, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to AC and saves against creatures you consider an ally and creatures who are [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=96) by you. If a creature you thought was an ally reveals itself as an enemy, you get the same bonus against them until the end of your next turn.

You make your living as a pirate, as well as a little extra by hiring out your services to Andoran, Cheliax, or Mbe’ke. You need to recognize which ships are legitimate targets and which you need to play nice with. You can use [Sailing Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) about creatures native to the High Seas and flags, ships, and sailors in the region. **Prerequisites**

**Access**
You're from the Shackles

</column>

---

An animal has become your loyal ally, perhaps after you liberated it from another ship or found it on a remote island. You gain the [Pet](/Feats.aspx?ID=5186) general feat. Your pet gains an additional pet Shackles Options ability, which you can choose from the standard pet abilities or the following familiar abilities: [accompanist](/Familiars.aspx?ID=108), [damage avoidance](/Familiars.aspx?ID=110), [independent](/Familiars.aspx?ID=115), [partner in crime](/Familiars.aspx?ID=119), [speech](/Familiars.aspx?ID=124), and [valet](/Familiars.aspx?ID=128). 

In addition, you learn a common 1st- or 2nd-rank spell that targets your familiar, and can cast it once per day as a [primal](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=4) [innate spell](/Rules.aspx?ID=2232). You can instead learn [_phase familiar_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1884) and can cast it once per hour as a primal innate spell; it’s not a focus spell for you. When you cast the chosen spell, you target your pirate’s pet instead of a familiar.
name: Pirate's Pet

As you fall, you grab onto an enemy using your hands or legs, and pull them down with you. Attempt an Athletics check against the triggering creature’s Reflex DC. On a success, the creature falls with you (though it can still attempt to Grab an Edge) or is also knocked prone.

<trait label="Swashbuckler" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=321" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [High Seas](/Sources.aspx?ID=351) pg. 93

**Access**
You're from the Shackles

**Requirements**
A rope is within your reach, or you have a [rope](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2748) or [grappling](/Traits.aspx?ID=619) weapon in your hand.

</column>

---

You’ve learned to fight confidently while swinging from a line. You take hold of a nearby rope, throw a rope from your hand, or fire a grappling weapon at a solid surface, and then swing up to twice your Speed. You can make a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) using a one-handed weapon or unarmed attack at any point during this movement. If you critically fail on this Strike, your movement ends at the point you attempted the Strike.

**Special** If you have [Pirate Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6378) and you boarded or disembarked from a boat or similar vehicle during this movement, the Strike deals one additional weapon damage die.

    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Magic Warrior Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=903) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [World Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=6) pg. 95

**Archetype** [Magic Warrior](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=19)

**Prerequisites**
ability to cast focus spells

**Access**
You are from the Mwangi Expanse.

</column>

---

You have taken up a nameless mask and sworn the oath of the magic warriors. You become trained in your choice of [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) or [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) and in Magic Warrior [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8); if you were already trained in the skill, you become an expert instead.

 You hide your identity behind a mask representing an animal of your choice, corresponding to one of the general animal types in the [_animal form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=10) spell. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saves against [divination](/Traits.aspx?ID=47) effects, though sometimes refusing to remove your mask can cause issues in areas that don't respect or understand the magic warrior tradition.

 Once you take this feat, if another creature ever learns your true face or name, you lose your abilities from this archetype. Close allies who knew of your decision to take the mask before your dedication don't break this taboo unless they tell someone else. To regain your abilities, you must discard your mask and obtain a new one of a different animal, then retrain Magic Warrior Dedication into a new Magic Warrior Dedication with your new mask. Your focus spells from the magic warrior archetype are the same tradition as your other spells (choose one if you have spells from multiple traditions).

**Special** You cannot select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the magic warrior archetype.

<title level="2">Magic Warrior Dedication leads to...</title>
[Magic Warrior Aspect](/Feats.aspx?ID=904), [Magic Warrior Transformation](/Feats.aspx?ID=905), [Nameless Anonymity](/Feats.aspx?ID=906)

</column>

---

You’re as skilled in combat underwater as on land. You gain the [Underwater Marauder](/Feats.aspx?ID=5230) skill feat, and when you roll a success on an Athletics check to [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=2381), you get a critical success instead. In addition, checks to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) or [Force Open](/Actions.aspx?ID=2375) nets you use are attempted against your class DC instead of the listed DC, and you can keep hold of a target you’ve grappled with a net with one hand.

<title level="2">Marine Marauder Dedication leads to...</title>
[Aquatic Passage](/Feats.aspx?ID=9036), [Aquatic Pirouette](/Feats.aspx?ID=9031), [Concealing Currents](/Feats.aspx?ID=9037), [Like a Fish in Water](/Feats.aspx?ID=9032), [Marine Combat Training](/Feats.aspx?ID=9033), [Marine Jet](/Feats.aspx?ID=9041), [Pressure Change](/Feats.aspx?ID=9039), [Reactive Tangle](/Feats.aspx?ID=9034), [Reel 'Em In](/Feats.aspx?ID=9042), [Shark Attack](/Feats.aspx?ID=9038), [Stay Here!](/Feats.aspx?ID=9040), [Surface Rush](/Feats.aspx?ID=9035), [Take in the Catch](/Feats.aspx?ID=9043)

You can flip open a book to simultaneously study and deflect attacks. When you [Raise a Shield](/Actions.aspx?ID=2316), you can raise a book you’re wielding instead of a [shield](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=12). While you have a book raised, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to AC and a +1 circumstance bonus to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) checks to identify creatures using a skill related to the subject of the book ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) if you’re using your spellbook). If consulting the book normally grants an item bonus to the check for consulting the book, you gain this bonus as well.

If you have [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=5212), you can use a raised tome for that feat as though it were a shield. The tome has Hardness 3, HP 12, and BT 6.

In addition, you can inscribe the [_reinforcing rune_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2811) into your spellbook to strengthen your tomes, using the same process as [transferring a rune](/Rules.aspx?ID=3166). The rune takes the form of a specialized diagram in your spellbook, occupying one page. The rune’s benefits apply to any one tome in your possession chosen during your daily preparations. If your spellbook leaves your possession, the rune-granting benefit is suppressed until you get the book back.

When you [Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=755) with a spell that has an area of a [burst](/Rules.aspx?ID=2385), [cone](/Rules.aspx?ID=2386), or [line](/Rules.aspx?ID=2388), the spell creates an area instead of affecting only the target. The target must be in the area, and Expansive Spellstrike has no effect if your spell was disrupted (such as if you critically fail your [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167)). A burst is centered on any corner you choose of the target’s square (or the corner of any square in its space for a Large or larger creature). A cone or line emits from you and must include the target; if you’re not adjacent to the target (using a [reach](/Traits.aspx?ID=684) weapon or [starlit span](/HybridStudies.aspx?ID=4), for example), choose any square adjacent to the target as the source. The spell affects all creatures in the area as normal, but the Strike still targets only one creature.

A burst is centered on any corner you choose of the target’s square (or the corner of any square in its space for a Large or larger creature). A cone or line emits from you and must include the target; if you’re not adjacent to the target (using a reach weapon or starlit span, for example), choose any square adjacent to the target as the source. The spell affects all creatures in the area as normal, but the Strike still targets only one creature.

You’ve magically constructed an extradimensional sheath for your weapon that you access through your clothing, typically through a pocket, sleeve, or seam. This sheath is hard to notice, granting a +2 circumstance bonus to your [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) checks to [Conceal an Item](/Actions.aspx?ID=2403) within it. A spirit sheath can hold up to 1 Bulk worth of weapons.

During a [Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=755), you can [Interact](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297) to draw one weapon from the sheath before you [Cast the Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734). You can draw or return a weapon to a spirit sheath as an Interact action, as can anyone else holding or wearing the clothing that contains the sheath. A [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1493) spell or similar effect can be used against the spirit sheath to expel the weapon. The [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) check is made against your spell DC and the counteract rank is half your level rounded up. The weapon is also expelled if you become [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95).

Attaching a scroll requires using the [Affix a Talisman](/Actions.aspx?ID=2632) action. You can have only one scroll affixed to a weapon at a time, and you can’t have both a talisman and scroll attached.

You’ve studied the [staff](/Weapons.aspx?ID=367) extensively to learn the hidden capabilities of your chosen weapon. When you critically succeed at an attack roll using a staff, you can apply the [critical specialization](/Rules.aspx?ID=2203) effect of the [club](/Weapons.aspx?ID=357) group. (If you use the critical specialization on a [Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=755), the spell still affects the target even if you pushed the target out of reach.) 

While you’re in [Arcane Cascade](/Actions.aspx?ID=756) stance, your staff gains the [deadly d6](/Traits.aspx?ID=570) trait, with the damage from the deadly die being the same damage type as the extra damage from Arcane Cascade.

In addition, you can place [property runes](/Rules.aspx?ID=3168) into a magic staff you prepare, even though a magic staff can’t typically hold property runes. You must first inscribe the property runes into your spellbook, using the same process as [transferring a rune](/Rules.aspx?ID=3166). The rune takes the form of a specialized diagram in your [spellbook](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2753), occupying one page. You can’t inscribe runes that can’t be placed on a non-magical staff, nor can you inscribe the [_shifting_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2846) rune. When you prepare a staff, you can impart any number of property runes from your spellbook into the staff, up to the limit imposed by the staff’s [_weapon potency_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2830) rune.
name: Student of the Staff

You can magically fuse a [shield](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=12) into your favorite book during your daily preparations or as a 10-minute activity with the [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645) trait. The shield appears in the book as an elaborate bookmark. The fusion lasts until you fuse a shield into a new book or the book is out of your possession for 24 hours. While the two are fused, the book shares the Hardness, Hit Points, and Broken Threshold of the shield. The fused item has the shield’s activations and benefits (such as a [_spellguard shield_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2826)’s bonus to saving throws against magic), and it can still be consulted as normal for purposes like [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) and the benefits of [Raise a Tome](/Feats.aspx?ID=2848). If the shield or your spellbook is etched with a [_reinforcing rune_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2811), the fused item gains the rune while they’re fused; if both have the rune, the highest-level rune applies.
name: Shielded Tome

<traits>
<trait label="Arcane" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=11" />
<trait label="Force" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=75" />
<trait label="Magus" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=953" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 21

**Prerequisites**
Your [Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=755) is charged, and you have at least one spell prepared in a spell slot.

</column>

---

Instead of blending a spell into an attack, you can funnel the spell’s magic into a pure blast that expands out from you. You smash your weapon or fist into the ground and expend a spell prepared in one of your spell slots. The magic of the spell explodes out in your choice of a 20-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387), 30-foot [cone](/Rules.aspx?ID=2386), or 60-foot [line](/Rules.aspx?ID=2388). Each creature in the area takes 1d10 force damage per spell rank of the expended spell, with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save against your spell DC. If your weapon has the [shove](/Traits.aspx?ID=694) trait, you push any creature that fails its save 10 feet; if your weapon has the [trip](/Traits.aspx?ID=716) trait, any creature that fails its save falls prone. Your [Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=755) is no longer charged.

If the spell you expended could deal a type of damage other than force, you can change the explosion’s damage to that type and replace Spell Crash’s force trait with the corresponding trait.

text: Feat 8 Fused Staff Arcane Magus Source Impossible Magic pg. 21 You can use your arcane prowess to fuse a magical staff into a weapon during your daily preparations or as a 10-minute activity with the manipulate trait. The fusion lasts until you fuse the staff again or the weapon is out of your possession for 24 hours. The fused item has the staff’s activations and other benefits, and it can be used to cast spells if you prepare it. The staff and the weapon share their fundamental runes, using whichever weapon potency and whichever striking rune is higher level. If the staff has property runes, they’re suppressed while it’s fused. The item’s fused abilities work for you alone. A different wielder can use the weapon normally, but they don’t get the benefit of the shared runes and can’t use the staff’s spells or abilities.

**Requirements**

---

You attack in an arc and enact your spell against everyone you hit. Make a [Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=755), but roll separate [Strikes](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) to attack two creatures, each of whom must be within your melee reach and adjacent to each other. If your spell could affect two or more targets or would normally have an area, your spell affects whichever foes you hit, not just the first target; otherwise, choose one target to affect with the spell. As Spellstrike, Spell Swipe counts as two attacks for your multiple attack penalty, but the penalty doesn’t increase until after you make both attacks. 

If you’re using a weapon that has the sweep trait, its circumstance bonus applies against both targets. You can use this activity with only melee Strikes, even if you have the [starlit span](/HybridStudies.aspx?ID=4) hybrid study or a similar ability. 

If you use [Expansive Spellstrike](/Feats.aspx?ID=2849) to Spellstrike with an area spell, apply the area as described in Expansive Spellstrike, choosing one of the two targets to determine the area.

Your Hellknight training teaches you to terrorize others into compliance, but you also study the structure and hierarchy of Hell. You must survive painful tests of your body and mind called reckonings, which steady your mind against all sorts of trauma. You gain resistance to mental damage equal to 1 + your number of class feats from the Hellknight Armiger archetype and other Hellknight archetypes. You become trained in [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) and Hell [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8); if you were already trained, you become an expert instead.

**Requirements**
Your last action was a successful Spellstrike, and the spell you cast dealt energy damage ([acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524), [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555), [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604), [force](/Traits.aspx?ID=610), [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697), [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509), or [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510)).

</column>

---

Magical energy spills out to extend beyond the creature you struck. The flowing energy forms a ray with a range of 120 feet originating from the creature you damaged. You can’t target any of the creatures you damaged with your [Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=755) with the ray. Make a spell attack against the new target’s AC, at the same multiple attack penalty as the Strike. On a hit, the target of the ray takes 1d4 damage per spell rank of the spell you used for Spellstrike, or 1d8 damage per rank if you cast the spell from a spell slot. The ray uses the same damage type as the spell dealt (choose one if it dealt more than one type of damage). This ray has the attack trait, the tradition trait of the original spell, and the trait matching the damage type.

You have been trained to resist the manipulations of fiends, and your Hellknight discipline makes you difficult to influence. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saves against mental effects that specifically improve your attitude and to your Will DC against someone Coercing you, Demoralizing you, Making an Impression on you, or Making a Request of you.

 If a mental effect would compel you to act in a way that violates your Hellknight order’s tenets (as determined by the GM), you can attempt to break free from the effect as a reaction triggered by receiving the violating order, and you gain a new Will save against the effect. You can attempt this new save only once for a given effect, even if you are compelled to violate your order’s tenets multiple times.

Use your own spellcasting statistics for this spell, as you do for other spells you cast.

When you make a [Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=755), you can expend this special spell slot to immediately prepare and cast a spell from your spellbook at 2 ranks lower than the slot’s rank. </column>

---

You combine the might of a multitarget spell with a whirling flurry of attacks. You use [Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=755), making a melee [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) against each enemy within your reach instead of against one enemy. If your spell can affect multiple targets or normally has an area, your spell affects all foes you hit, not just the first target, up to the spell’s normal maximum targets. If you Strike more enemies than the spell could target, choose which foes are affected by the spell. Each attack counts toward your multiple attack penalty but doesn’t increase your penalty until you’ve made all your attacks.

You can use this activity with only melee Strikes, even if you have the [starlit span hybrid study](/HybridStudies.aspx?ID=4) or a similar ability. 

If you use [Expansive Spellstrike](/Feats.aspx?ID=2849) to Spellstrike with an area spell, apply the area as described in Expansive Spellstrike, choosing one of the targets to determine the area.
name: Whirlwind Spell

If you have bones, you have a weapon. You create a _[+1 striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) weapon_ in which you are proficient, made of bone and sinew. If this weapon requires [ammunition](/Rules.aspx?ID=3193), mundane bone ammunition is created when you [reload](/Rules.aspx?ID=2196) it. The weapon falls apart and is destroyed after 1 hour, if you aren’t holding the weapon at the end of your turn, or if you use this action again, whichever comes first. 

At 8th level, you can destroy an adjacent thrall as part of using this action. If you do, the action gains the [thrall](/Traits.aspx?ID=955) trait and the weapon also gains a [_decaying_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2835) rune, or the _greater decaying_ rune if you’re 15th level or higher.

At 10th level, the weapon improves to a _+2 striking weapon_, increasing to a _+2 greater striking weapon_ at 12th level, a _+3 greater striking weapon_ at 16th level, or a _+3 major striking weapon_ at 19th level.

Whether through blood (if you’re Varisian, Shoanti, or New Thassilonian) or by exposure to rune magic, you have become runescarred, with visible, glowing runes on your body in the form of tattoos or scars.  Choose one cantrip from the [arcane](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=1) list. One of the runes on your body corresponds to the chosen cantrip, and you can cast the chosen cantrip as an innate arcane spell.

You gain [lifesense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=67) as an [imprecise sense](/Rules.aspx?ID=2407) with a range of 30 feet. This allows you to sense the life force of living and [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) creatures within the listed range. You channel the essences and echoes of spirits long dead that reside within a location, an object, or a bloodline. You spend 10 minutes and must be within the location, be able to touch a piece of the object, or drink a drop of blood of the bloodline as appropriate to the spirits you wish to channel. You learn one piece of information or about one significant event relating directly to the location, object, or bloodline that has occurred within the last year. You can channel any given target only once every 24 hours.

At 12th level, you can learn about information or events that took place within the last decade, within the last century if you are 16th level, or at any point in history at 20th level.

You create a fleshy eyeball that is the size of a marble. You can take a single action, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) trait, to look through any of your eyeballs until the start of your next turn. An eyeball can be manipulated like a marble, such as being rolled or thrown. One can also be affixed to a surface, for example a wall, with 1 minute’s work. An eyeball lasts for 24 hours, and you can maintain a total of three eyeballs at any given time. Creating a fourth destroys the oldest eyeball. 

Eyeballs are very small but are easy to spot. A creature actively [Seeking](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) or [Searching](/Actions.aspx?ID=2630) automatically finds an eyeball. They’re also not very sturdy and can be destroyed with an [Interact](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297) action.

[Final Union](/Feats.aspx?ID=9162) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Necromancer" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=950" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 41

**Prerequisites**
[Bind Heroic Spirit](/Feats.aspx?ID=9114)

</column>

---

You and the heroic spirit have formed an eternal pact and now share your body. You are constantly under the effect of a 10th-rank bind heroic spirit. You choose whether the heroic spirit remains as a separate entity bound to you or whether you become a fused spirit that lives in unison, possibly identifying as an entirely new person.

You gain the [Additional Lore](/Feats.aspx?ID=5114) feat for a topic the spirit knew in life, usually [Warfare Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41).

If you would fall [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95), you don’t fall [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88) or drop any items. Instead, your heroic spirit takes control of your body, allowing you to perform actions as if you were still conscious. If you would die, your heroic spirit puppets your corpse for up to 1 minute after your death or until your body is destroyed. While dead, you are an undead object, granting you [immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=1609) to [bleed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86), [death effects](/Rules.aspx?ID=2331), [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623), [nonlethal attacks](/Rules.aspx?ID=2311), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), and [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510), as well as the [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67), [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68), [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=73), [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91), and unconscious conditions. As an object, you have 200 Hit Points and a [Broken](/Conditions.aspx?ID=60) Threshold of 100 Hit Points. While broken, you are [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1. If you are destroyed, your body must be mended before you can be brought back to life. A creature can spend 8 hours to attempt a DC 45 [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) check, mending your body on a success. Alternatively, powerful magic such as the [_remake_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1649) spell or the [_wish_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=125) ritual can also be used to mend your body.
name: Final Union

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Necromancer" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=950" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
<trait label="Unholy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=521" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 41

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
You are [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521).

</column>

---

You attempt to steal the soul of a creature that was at least 18th level that died within the last minute. Attempt an [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) check against the hard DC of the [target’s level](/Rules.aspx?ID=2629). On a success, you capture its soul and solidify it into a gem that keeps the soul contained. While the soul is contained, it can’t be returned to life through any means, even powerful magic such as the [_wish_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=125) ritual. If a gem is destroyed, the soul is freed, and you become alerted to its destruction. You can maintain only three gems at any given time. If you attempt to make a fourth, you must choose a soul to be released. 

You can consume a captured soul by swallowing a gem. Doing so grants you the [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521) and [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) traits and extends your existence by 50 years. You gain [void healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=83), you aren’t instantly destroyed when reduced to 0 Hit Points, and you can’t be instantly killed by [death effects](/Rules.aspx?ID=2331). If you’re destroyed, you can rebuild yourself in the location of one of your soul gems. This consumes the gem, and it takes 24 hours for your body to be rebuilt. If you are ever destroyed and are unable to rebuild your body, all souls that you have consumed are released.
name: Soul Thief

You practice the lost art of using music to guide your runecarving, singing the runes into existence as much as crafting them. You can use Performance instead of [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) when attempting Crafting checks related to runes.

Once per 10 minutes, you can [Trace a Rune](/Actions.aspx?ID=4264) with song alone. You don't need to be able to move your hands when Tracing a Rune using song, but you do need to be able to sing in a clear voice.
