You are well-versed in the use of magical runes in traps and hazards. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=3303) checks to find magical traps. Even if you aren’t [Searching](/Actions.aspx?ID=2630), you get a check to find magical traps that normally require you to be Searching. You still need to meet any other requirements to find the trap. As long as you are holding or wearing an [artisan’s toolkit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2703), you can use [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) instead of [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) to disable a magical trap, treating your proficiency in Crafting as your proficiency in Thievery for requirements.

In addition, if you trigger a trap by critically failing a check to [Disable](/Actions.aspx?ID=2411) it, you can [Trace a Rune](/Actions.aspx?ID=4264) on yourself as a reaction, gaining the benefits of the rune before the trap affects you.
name: Seek the Hidden Glyphs

<column gap="tiny">

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), Expert in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43), Expert in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44), or Expert in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)

</column>

---

You place hidden messages written in a runic cipher of your devising. You can cast [_embed message_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1511) once per day as an [innate spell](/Rules.aspx?ID=2232). The rank of this spell is equal to half your level, rounded up, and the tradition can be any tradition for which you are at least expert in the related skill (Arcana for [arcane](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=1), Nature for [primal](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=4), Occultism for [occult](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=3), and Religion for [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2)). When you cast _embed message_, instead of choosing a language you know for the message’s text and speech, you can choose to have the message be text only, written in a runic code that only you know. You can impart the knowledge of this code to up to 5 creatures over the course of 10 minutes; they retain this knowledge indefinitely, but you can devise a new runic code for subsequent messages you wish to be encoded.

A creature can [Decipher the Writing](/Actions.aspx?ID=2363) of your runic code using the same skill associated with the chosen tradition against your class DC.

When you apply a rune to a foe, it reveals something about them to you. [Trace a Rune](/Actions.aspx?ID=4264) onto an adjacent enemy and then attempt a skill check to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) about that target. If you succeed, you leverage this knowledge when you invoke any of your runes on that target; that target takes a –1 status penalty to saving throws against your invocations for 1 minute. You touch an adjacent [_corrosive_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2834), [_flaming_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2838), [_frost_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2839), [_shock_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2847), or [_thundering_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2850) rune on an unattended item or one held or worn by a willing creature, and you change it to any other rune from that list. You see the thin lines of magic between your creations, and you can exploit that connection with a small shift of power from one rune to another. You [Invoke two Runes](/Actions.aspx?ID=4265) within 60 feet. In addition to the runes’ normal effects, a chain of glowing script flows between them, dealing 5d6 force damage to all creatures in a straight [line](/Rules.aspx?ID=2388) between them with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex saving throw; creatures bearing the invoked runes are not in the area of this line. The DC to Escape is your class DC. 

At 12th level, and every 2 levels thereafter, the damage increases by 1d6.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Runesmith" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=952" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 51

**Prerequisites**
Master in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), Master in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43), Master in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44), or Master in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)

</column>

---

You can write a message that travels long distances at the speed of thought. Once per day, you can take 1 minute to write a message of 25 words or fewer anywhere that can, at least momentarily, hold writing (such as on a piece of parchment, drawn in the sand, or lightly scratched onto soft metal). When you are finished, mentally picture one creature you know well. If the target creature is on the same plane as you, your message appears in their line of sight on any surface that can hold writing. It can be seen by only the target, and the target can read the message even if you don’t share a language. The message disappears once the target reads it, but the creature can respond by spending 1 minute to write their own message of 25 words or fewer in the same way. You instantly receive that message when it is finished, and you can read it even if you don’t share a language.

If you spend 10 minutes writing your message instead, you can include a rune from your runic repertoire. If the target is willing, after reading your message, you Trace the Rune on the target to last for up to 10 minutes. When you receive the creature’s reply, you can Invoke that Rune as a free action.

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 52

</column>

---

You create a runestone that floats around you, and you [Trace a Rune](/Actions.aspx?ID=4264) with a damaging invocation on it even if the rune could not normally be applied to an object. The runestone has 10 Hit Points. Each time a creature successfully [Strikes](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) you, attempt a DC 11 [flat check](/Rules.aspx?ID=333). On a success, the runestone blocks the attack, so the attack first damages the runestone and then applies any remaining damage to you. If this damage reduces the runestone to 0 Hit Points, it explodes outward toward the attacker. If the attacker is within 15 feet, the rune etched upon the runestone invokes automatically, applying its invocation effect to the attacker. The attacker is the only one affected by the invocation, even if the rune could normally affect multiple creatures.

The runestone’s magic is capable of maintaining the traced rune for up to 1 minute as it floats around you, at which point the rune fades and the runestone shatters. You can maintain only a single orbiting rune at any given time. If you try to create a second, the first one shatters.
name: Orbiting Runestone

<traits>

[Lion Blade Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=917)

---

You’ve learned how to analyze and fake your responses to the most common magic used against spies. Whenever you succeed at your save against a divination or mental effect, you can Identify Magic to identify the spell as a free action triggered when you succeed, even if you didn’t notice the spell being cast. If you successfully identify a divination effect targeting you and the spell would normally fail or have no effect, you can create a substitute result, causing the spell’s caster to think the spell succeeded, with a result of your choice. If you successfully identify a mental effect targeting you and the spell would normally fail or have no effect, you can make it appear as if you were affected and attempt to play along with the spell; if the spell normally establishes a mental link, it functions normally but you can disregard any commands you receive through the link.
name: Spy's Countermeasures

You can trap a foe in a twisting, extradimensional labyrinth of ever-shifting runes. You can cast [_quandary_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1644) once per day as an [innate spell](/Rules.aspx?ID=2232). The rank of this spell is equal to half your level rounded up, and the tradition can be any tradition for which you are at least legendary in the related skill. Instead of the usual skill checks to solve the puzzle, the target of your _quandary_ can attempt a [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=2040) check, a [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) check to [Decipher Writing](/Actions.aspx?ID=2363), or a check in the skill related to the tradition of the spell. When you [Sustain](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317) this spell, you can also [Trace a Rune](/Actions.aspx?ID=4264) or [Invoke one Rune](/Actions.aspx?ID=4265) on the target creature as if it were adjacent to you.

The rank of this spell is equal to half your level rounded up, and the tradition can be any tradition for which you are at least legendary in the related skill. Instead of the usual skill checks to solve the puzzle, the target of your quandary can attempt a Perception check, a Society check to Decipher Writing, or a check in the skill related to the tradition of the spell. When you Sustain this spell, you can also Trace a Rune or Invoke one Rune on the target creature as if it were adjacent to you.

Each tradition of magic holds sway over two of the four essences that make up all of creation, and so by invoking runes from each tradition at once, you can pull from the four corners of magic to unravel anything. You [invoke four runes](/Actions.aspx?ID=4265) of your choice, each of which must be from a different tradition of magic. In addition to the runes’ normal effects, one creature within 30 feet of all invoked runes must attempt a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Fortitude saving throw, taking 10d4 force damage on a failure as destructive magical reverberations clash in their body. The creature’s gear is unharmed.

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 53

</column>

---

At the pinnacle of your art, you have forged a new great rune of power, a new ideal expression or utterance to be added to the craft. You create a rune and add it to your runic repertoire. When you gain this feat, choose a spell of 4th rank or lower. It must be common, or you must otherwise have access to it. The spell must take 1 or 2 actions to cast. You can choose a variable action spell, deciding when you create the rune whether the rune uses the 1-action or 2-action version of the spell. Name your rune. This rune has the [unique](/Traits.aspx?ID=723) trait and a [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644) trait of your choosing ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662), or [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)). 

This rune can be drawn on a creature or object, regardless of what the spell can target. When invoked, this rune has the effect of the chosen spell. The rune-bearer is the point of origin for the spell’s effect; calculate range and cover from its space. If the spell has targets, you decide who or what the spell targets, and the rune-bearer is a possible target if your chosen spell can target it. If the spell can affect only you (such as [_translocate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1724)), invoking it affects only you, and has no effect if the rune is drawn anywhere other than on you. If the spell requires a spell attack roll, use your class DC – 10 in place of the spell attack modifier. If your chosen spell has a duration and that duration is longer than 1 minute, the invoked rune’s duration is 1 minute instead.
name: Forge New Word

</traits>

</column>

---

Your physical form can combine with that of your eidolon. You Manifest your Eidolon, but instead of summoning them into an adjacent open space, you become them. You can also Meld into Eidolon while your eidolon is manifested in an adjacent space. While Manifested in this way, you use your eidolon’s statistics, and you can’t act except to direct the eidolon to use Manifest an Eidolon to unmanifest themself. Your eidolon is affected by [_boost eidolon_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1045) while Manifested in this way.

Since you can’t act, you can’t cast spells, activate or benefit from magic items that normally benefit you and not your eidolon, perform actions that have the [tandem](/Traits.aspx?ID=395) trait, or use other abilities that require you, and not the eidolon, to act. You can’t be separately targeted while you are melded into the eidolon. When you reach 0 HP, your eidolon unmanifests, leaving your body behind, [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95) and [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69).
name: Meld Into Eidolon

Your separate experiences in different societies have evolved into entirely separate lives. Create a second identity for yourself with a different name, history, and background. Your eidolon changes to make them particularly effective as your mount. While you ride them, you get your full number of actions each round instead of reducing them to 2. This applies only when you ride your eidolon, not when anyone else does (see the Riding Sapient Creatures sidebar). Your eidolon still must be at least one size category larger than you to ride them. Since you work together to move, your eidolon’s move actions while you’re mounted gain the [tandem](/Traits.aspx?ID=395) trait.

<title level="3">Riding Sapient Creatures</title> Riding along on a sapient creature that isn’t a minion requires a lot of coordination and timing. Both the riding creature and the mount regain only 2 actions at the start of their turns each round, as both the mount and the riding creature interfere with one another’s actions. If you ride your eidolon, you reduce your total actions to 2 and continue to share actions normally—you don’t reduce the number of actions twice.
name: Steed Form

>
[Reveal Machinations](/Feats.aspx?ID=924) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Age of Ashes</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #147: Tomorrow Must Burn](/Sources.aspx?ID=8) pg. 73

**Prerequisites**
Legendary in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5)

</column>

---

You reveal that you played a minor but recurring role in another humanoid’s life—or at least convince them that’s the case. Attempt a [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) check against the target’s Will DC. On a success, the revelation makes them [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19) 2, and on a critical success they are frightened 3. In addition, you gain information about the subject as though you had attempted to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) about them using an appropriate skill and received the same result on your roll. You can’t use this ability against the same humanoid again until 1 day has passed and you’ve also successfully disguised yourself as a different person.

**Special** At the GM’s discretion, this feat can be used against non-humanoids if they have regular contact with humanoids or you are able to disguise yourself as a member of the target’s ancestry or type of creature.

<title level="2">Lacunafex Lore</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #147: Tomorrow Must Burn](/Sources.aspx?ID=8) pg. 72

If the PCs earn Mialari Docur's trust and prove their worth by defeating the Scarlet Triad, she rewards them by granting them access to several feats and spells she and her students have developed over the years.

**Related Feats**: [Different Worlds](/Feats.aspx?ID=923), [Secret Speech](/Feats.aspx?ID=925), [Silver's Refrain](/Feats.aspx?ID=926), [Tweak Appearances](/Feats.aspx?ID=927)
name: Reveal Machinations

---

Choose a secret society (such as the Lacunafex or the Bellflower Network). You’ve learned that society’s secret cant or jargon, enabling you to share hidden messages when signing or speaking with others who’ve also learned it. If an observer succeeds at a Perception check against your [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) DC when you do this, they realize you are passing a message but fail to discern its content, unless they subsequently succeed at a Society check against your Deception DC. On a critical success, they learn not only the message, but also who you’re passing the message to.

Your eidolon’s attack provides you an opening for one of your spells. Your eidolon makes a melee [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) against a creature, and then you cast a 1- or 2-action cantrip targeting the same creature. If your eidolon’s Strike hits, the creature is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) against your spell (if it requires a spell attack roll) or takes a –2 circumstance penalty to its save against your spell (if it requires a saving throw). If your eidolon’s Strike and the spell deal the same type of damage, combine the damage of both for the purpose of resistances and weaknesses. Both your eidolon’s attack and any spell attack roll you make count toward your multiple attack penalty, but the penalty doesn’t increase until after both attacks have been made.
name: Magical Onslaught

---

You dedicate yourself to freeing slaves and escorting them to freedom. You gain a +5-foot status bonus to your Speed. Choose up to six other people to be your “crop.” Members of your crop can use your Speed for overland travel if it’s higher than their own. Members more than 60 feet from you lose all benefits (from this or other Bellflower tiller feats) of being part of your crop, but they regain those benefits immediately when they return. You can add or remove someone from your crop by spending 10 minutes in conversation with them.

**Special** You cannot select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the Bellflower tiller archetype.

<title level="2">Bellflower Dedication leads to...</title>

You can transform to match your eidolon. When you [Manifest your Eidolon](/Actions.aspx?ID=757), you can call upon their powers to transform yourself into a duplicate until your eidolon unmanifests. You can’t use this if you Manifest your Eidolon in an unusual way, such as [Meld into Eidolon](/Feats.aspx?ID=2892). While using Twin Eidolon, you use your eidolon’s statistics other than your own Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma attribute modifiers, including their evolutions. You can’t cast spells (except spells your eidolon could cast), Activate or otherwise benefit from magic items that normally benefit you and not your eidolon, or use other actions they can’t perform. Any of their spells you cast with limited uses count against your eidolon’s uses. You can Manifest your Eidolon again to end this effect.

**Special** This feat has the trait matching your eidolon’s tradition ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662), or [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)).

You become trained in runesmith [class DC](/Rules.aspx?ID=2051) and [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37). You gain a [runic repertoire](/RunesmithRunes.aspx) with two 1st-level runes of your choice. You choose these from the common runes on the rune list as well as uncommon or rarer runes you have access to. 

You can etch runes. An etched rune is carved, inked, or branded; this application does not damage the creature or item. Etching a rune requires an artisan's toolkit. Your magic can sustain up to one etched rune at a time. If you're at least 9th level, increase the maximum number of etched runes you can sustain at a time to 2, and if you're at least 17th level, increase it to 3. You can etch any number of runes up to your maximum during your daily preparations or by spending 10 minutes in exploration mode. Your etched runes remain indefinitely until they're expended or removed or until you etch more runes than your maximum, which causes your oldest rune to fade. Additionally, you gain the Solitary Invocation action. 

**Solitary Invocation** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([invocation](/Traits.aspx?ID=956), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [runesmith](/Traits.aspx?ID=952)) You utter the name of one of your runes within 30 feet, which blazes with power, applying the effect in its Invocation entry. An invoked rune then fades away, its task complete.

**Prerequisites**
Charisma +2

</column>

---

You’ve formed a bond with an eidolon, an entity that manifests in a physical body only through their link to your life force. You gain an [eidolon](/Eidolons.aspx) as well as the [Manifest Eidolon](/Actions.aspx?ID=757) activity. Due to your tenuous link, you can’t gain or use [tandem](/Traits.aspx?ID=395) actions. Because you don’t have [Act Together](/Actions.aspx?ID=758), only you or your eidolon can perform an [exploration](/Rules.aspx?ID=2006) activity at one time. 

Your eidolon is trained in unarmed attacks and unarmored defense, and shares your proficiency rank for [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=2040), saving throws, and skill checks. Choose an eidolon type. You become trained in your eidolon’s listed skills. For each of those skills that you’re already trained in, you become trained in a different skill of your choice. Your eidolon’s initial attributes are reduced. Instead of starting with a +4 attribute modifier in Strength or Dexterity and +2 in the other, your eidolon starts with a +3 in Strength or Dexterity and +2 in the other attribute. They otherwise gain the statistics listed for an eidolon of that type. 

At 5th level, the eidolon’s attribute modifier that was reduced to +3 increases to +4, before applying attribute boosts. At levels 5, 10, 15, and 20, your eidolon also gets four attribute boosts, which follow the same rules as yours.

<title level="2">Summoner Dedication leads to...</title>
[Basic Summoner Spellcasting](/Feats.aspx?ID=9308), [Basic Synergy](/Feats.aspx?ID=9309), [Expert Combat Eidolon](/Feats.aspx?ID=9312), [Initial Eidolon Ability](/Feats.aspx?ID=9310)
name: Summoner Dedication

You’re so charming and distracting that when pressed, you can cast a simple charm in time to foil an attacker. You can cast one of your [innate 1st-rank spells](/Rules.aspx?ID=2901) with the [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) trait that normally takes two actions or fewer to cast as a reaction. This takes effect before the triggering spell or attack, and if the attacker is affected by your spell, it can make different decisions for its attack or spell (for instance, if you charm the attacker, it can choose a different target than you for its attack or spell). The attacking creature must be in range of your chosen spell, and if your spell requires targets, the attacking creature must be a valid target. Your spell affects only the attacking creature, even if it would normally affect more targets or an area.
name: Reactive Charm

If your charms or illusions fail to ensnare the minds of others, you can cast them again. You must use the same number of actions to recast the same spell on your following turn; if you can’t, or choose not to, you lose the spell. After this second casting, you lose the spell whether it affected any targets or not, and you can’t use Look Again until your next daily preparations. Look Again works only with spells that can affect creatures or require a target and doesn’t do anything if you cast the spell with no targets or creatures in the area.

[Hedge Mage Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=9326) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 94

**Archetype** [Hedge Mage](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=391)

**Prerequisites**
Intelligence +2 or Wisdom +2

</column>

---

[The Universe](/Planes.aspx?ID=26) is your laboratory and altar, and the world your workshop and study. Grounding your theoretical studies in honest labor, you work with the mundane to draw forth their hidden magic. When you take this dedication, choose [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43), [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44), or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46). You become trained in that skill, or you become expert if you were already trained. You also gain a keepsake that helps your magical studies; this keepsake is something that has perhaps been handed down to you but to which you’ve contributed a few personal touches, though it can be anything appropriate to your personal magical style. Sample keepsakes include a folio or binder of magical observations, a walking stick with mnemonic grooves, a bracelet of assorted charms and baubles, or a planchette carved into shape of a coffin. If it’s destroyed or lost, you can create a new keepsake with 1 day of downtime.

You gain the [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=3521) activity. You’re trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. Your key spellcasting attribute for hedge mage archetype spells is your choice of Intelligence or Wisdom, and they are hedge mage spells of a tradition associated with the skill chosen for this dedication ([arcane](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=1) for Arcana, [primal](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=4) for Nature, [occult](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=3) for Occultism, and [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2) for Religion).

Your keepsake holds 4 common cantrips of your choice from your appropriate tradition. You prepare spells each day by meditating with your keepsake. You can prepare two cantrips from your keepsake each day. You can only add cantrips to your keepsake with the [Learn a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2366) activity or by other similar means.

<title level="2">Hedge Mage Dedication leads to...</title>
[Basic Hedge Mage Spellcasting](/Feats.aspx?ID=9327), [Community Needs](/Feats.aspx?ID=9336), [Humble Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=9330), [Keepsake of Power](/Feats.aspx?ID=9334), [Peer Past the Hedge](/Feats.aspx?ID=9328), [Practical Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=9331), [Tender Ministrations](/Feats.aspx?ID=9329)
name: Hedge Mage Dedication

---

Want not, waste not; through a mix of frugality, inspiration, and sheer resourcefulness, you maintain a catalog of materials with ambient, lingering magic, which you can transform into temporary [spell catalysts](/Rules.aspx?ID=1509). Be it powder ground from the burnt remains of hippogriff feathers or yarn drawn from the locks of an [alicorn](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3320), you have these materials at hand and, perhaps more importantly, know how to bend them toward practical effects. These [consumable](/Traits.aspx?ID=564) items can change or enhance the effects of specific spells. To get the most out of a spell catalyst, you or an ally should be able to cast the affected spell.

You know the formulas for all common spell catalysts of your level or lower. You remember spell catalyst formulas and don’t need a formula book for them. Each day during your daily preparations, you can make two spell catalysts with an item level no higher than half your level. You must know each spell catalyst’s formula. A spell catalyst created this way is a temporary item and loses its magic the next time you make your [daily preparations](/Rules.aspx?ID=2575) if you haven’t already used it.
name: Practical Magic

You have learned to take the time needed to be flexible and to contemplate the best use of your magic for those around you. You can spend 10 minutes to empty one of your prepared spell slots and prepare a different spell from your keepsake in its place. If you’re interrupted during such a swap, the original spell remains prepared and can still be cast. You can try again to swap out the spell later, but you must start the process over again.

>
[Living Nexus Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=9338) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 96

**Archetype** [Living Nexus](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=392)

**Prerequisites**
trained in martial weapons; Trained in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), Trained in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43), Trained in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44), or Trained in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)

</column>

---

Whether through happenstance or hours of rigorous training, you have discovered within yourself the ability to breathe in the magic around you.

You have an invisible, internal nexus of energy and have learned how to control your absorption of others’ magical energy and store it in this internal nexus. You gain the Absorb Magic reaction and the Overflowing Blade action. The DC for an ability gained via this archetype is either your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher, and is called your nexus DC. 

**Absorb Magic** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644)) **Requirements** You are not overflowing; **Trigger** Another creature within 30 feet [Casts a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=3521) or uses an action, activity, or reaction with the [arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662), or [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676) trait; **Effect** You breathe in a small fraction of the magic produced by the triggering effect, storing it in your internal nexus. You become overflowing. You remain overflowing for up to 1 minute before the stored magical energy fades. While overflowing, you gain a +1 status bonus to saving throws against effects with the arcane, divine, magical, occult, and primal traits. This bonus becomes +2 at 15th level.

**Overflowing Blade** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [force](/Traits.aspx?ID=610), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644)) **Requirements** You are overflowing; **Effect** You conduct the magic in your internal nexus to coat your weapon or unarmed strike, empowering it with magical energy for a devastating attack. Make a melee [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167). If the Strike hits, you deal an additional 1d4 force damage. At 10th level, the additional damage increases to 2d4 force damage. At 18th level, the additional damage increases to 3d4 force damage. You are no longer overflowing.

<title level="2">Living Nexus Dedication leads to...</title>
[Aether Beam](/Feats.aspx?ID=9345), [Aether Blast](/Feats.aspx?ID=9340), [Flexible Nexus](/Feats.aspx?ID=9342), [Harness Natural Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=9343), [Healing Nexus](/Feats.aspx?ID=9346), [Inspired Memory](/Feats.aspx?ID=9339), [Null Field](/Feats.aspx?ID=9347), [Quick Absorption](/Feats.aspx?ID=9349), [Steal Magic's Breath](/Feats.aspx?ID=9348), [Surging Smash](/Feats.aspx?ID=9344), [The Taste of Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=9341)

Select a magical effect that has made an adjacent member of your crop clumsy, grabbed, paralyzed, restrained, or slowed. Attempt a counteract check using your attack modifier (including your multiple attack penalty) with a melee weapon with which you have expert proficiency. Your counteract level is half your level rounded up. On a success, you free that member from the effect; on a failure, you can’t attempt to use Cut the Bonds on that effect on that crop member until 24 hours have passed.

**Trigger**
You are the target or within the area of a damaging spell or ability with the [arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662), or [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676) trait.

Your internal nexus has grown to an immense size and can absorb workings of magic even as they form, sometimes even swallowing them entirely. You become overflowing as if you had Absorbed Magic. Additionally, you reduce the amount of damage the triggering spell or ability deals by 6d6 for all creatures targeted by the spell or ability. This reduction is applied before any [weaknesses](/Rules.aspx?ID=2317) or [resistances](/Rules.aspx?ID=2893) are taken into account. If you completely mitigate the damage to a creature, the triggering spell or ability has no effect on them.

The amount of damage reduced increases by 1d6 at 14th level and every 2 levels thereafter.

**Prerequisites**

</column>

---

You can manifest the power of your spirit in combat to realize your motivations. You bind a suit of armor, shield, or weapon as a [soulforged armament](/Rules.aspx?ID=3690). Choose a motivation or cause known as a soul path (page 101) that ties you to your soulforged armament; acting against or ignoring your soul path is anathema to you and could lead you to be afflicted with a curse called [soulforged corruption](/Rules.aspx?ID=3693). Choose one essence power for the armament (see archetype). Changing an essence power requires 1 week of retraining, and you can’t retrain them while you have soulforged corruption. 

You can Manifest Soulforged Armament to summon your soulforged armaments in combat. 

**Manifest Soulforged Armament** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [extradimensional](/Traits.aspx?ID=596)) **Requirements** If summoning a soulforged weapon or shield, you have the hands free to wield it; if summoning soulforged armor, you aren’t wearing any armor; **Effect** You immediately wield or wear the soulforged armament bound to you. The soulforged armament remains manifested until you [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311) this effect. 

Once per day when you use this ability, you can manifest the armament’s essence form. You gain the armament’s essence power until it’s Dismissed. After 1 minute, the essence form armament is automatically Dismissed.

<title level="2">Soulforger Dedication leads to...</title>
[Devastating Manifestation](/Feats.aspx?ID=9354), [Rapid Manifestation](/Feats.aspx?ID=9352), [Soul Arsenal](/Feats.aspx?ID=9353), [Soul Flare](/Feats.aspx?ID=9351)

>
[Soul Arsenal](/Feats.aspx?ID=9353) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 98

**Archetype** [Soulforger](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=393)

**Prerequisites**
[Soulforger Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=9350)

</column>

---

Choose an additional soulforged armament of a different type than you already chose, and choose one essence power for it. Upgrade or change your armaments individually.

When you Manifest Soulforged Armament, you can summon any number of your armaments (you must meet the requirements for each), and when you [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311) the effect, you can choose to Dismiss some and not others. You can choose to manifest the essence form of any number of your armaments when you take the action. Each armament can manifest its essence form only once per day.

When you gain soulforged corruption, you choose one armament’s corruption flaw to affect you for stage 1. At stage 2, you take the flaws of all your soulforged armaments. While you have the curse, each armament gets a separate [flat check](/Rules.aspx?ID=333) if you try to manifest its essence form, and failing the check prevents you from manifesting only that armament’s essence form.

**Special** You can select this feat a second time at 12th level, choosing the final item type.
name: Soul Arsenal

    right="Feat 14"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Devastating Manifestation](/Feats.aspx?ID=9354) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 98

**Archetype** [Soulforger](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=393)

**Prerequisites**
[Soulforger Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=9350)

**Requirements**
At least one of your soulforged armaments is not manifested.

</column>

---

Your armaments are especially powerful the moment after you manifest them. You Manifest Soulforged Armament. If you manifested a weapon, make up to two [Strikes](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) with that weapon, each targeting a different creature and each dealing an additional 1d6 spirit damage. Each attack counts toward your multiple attack penalty, but your penalty doesn’t increase until you have made all your attacks. If you Manifested an armor or shield, you gain [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) 5 to all damage until the start of your next turn. If you manifested both a weapon and an armor or shield, you gain both effects.
name: Devastating Manifestation
requirement: At least one of your soulforged armaments is not manifested.

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 102 **Archetype** [Spellshifter](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=394) **Prerequisites** Trained in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) --- You can exert your will over magical spells cast in your vicinity, potentially altering or controlling their effects. You accomplish this through the use of a spellshifting conduit, a magical object of your choice that has light Bulk and can be held in one hand. If your conduit is lost or destroyed, you can train yourself to use a new one by spending 10 minutes attuning yourself to it. You gain the Shift Spell action and the Share the Burden spellshift. **Shift Spell** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Requirements** You are within the affected area of an ongoing spell, or you can physically touch an object or creature under the effects of a spell, and you are holding your conduit; **Effect** Choose a spellshift and attempt an [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) check against the DC of the spell (or the spell DC of the spellcaster if the spell does not normally have a DC). The caster immediately becomes aware that you’re trying to shift their spell and intuitively knows the potential effects of the shift, but not the result of your skill check. A willing caster can allow you to achieve one degree of success higher than the result of your check. The effects of the check are dependent on the chosen spellshift. Regardless of the result, the spell becomes immune to Shift Spell for 24 hours. **Spellshift—Shift Burden** You share the burden of a spell, allowing you to share control with the caster. If [Sustaining](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317) a spell with this spellshift causes a creature to attempt a saving throw, it is attempted against the higher of your class DC or spell DC. If the spell requires a spell attack roll, make the attack using your Arcana modifier instead of the spell’s normal spell attack modifier. **Critical Success** If the spell is sustainable, you can [Sustain](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317) the spell as a free action as though you had cast the spell. For the remainder of the spell’s duration, you can Sustain the spell as though you were the caster.
**Success** If the spell is sustainable, you can Sustain the spell as a free action as though you had cast the spell. Spellshifter Dedication leads to... [Analyze Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=9356), [Dismantle Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=9359), [Elemental Subsitution](/Feats.aspx?ID=9357), [Enhance Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=9361), [Reactive Spellshift](/Feats.aspx?ID=9360), [Redirect Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=9362), [Subtle Shift](/Feats.aspx?ID=9358)
name: Spellshifter Dedication

You gain the Elemental Substitution spellshift. **Spellshift—Elemental Substitution** Raw elemental energy is the fuel powering some of the most iconic spells of destruction ever devised, and you’ve discovered a method for realigning the magical pathways through which that energy flows into the material world. **Critical Success** If the targeted spell inflicts [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524), [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555), [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604), or [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697) damage, you change its damage type to your choice of one of acid, cold, electricity, fire, or sonic damage. If the effect has a duration, it inflicts damage of its new type for 1 minute, then returns to normal.
**Success** As critical success, except if the effect has a duration, it inflicts damage of its new type until the beginning of your next turn, then returns to normal.

<traits>

---

You’ve learned how to hide your meddling from the casters of spells you’re shifting. If your [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) check when Shifting a Spell is greater than its caster’s [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=2040) DC, you can prevent the caster from learning the effects of the shift you’re attempting to apply. On a critical success, they don’t become aware that you’re applying a shift at all (although the effect of the shift might still give you away).
name: Subtle Shift

Select one willing ally within 30 feet that you can see and choose one of the following spellshape feats: [Conceal Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=4997), [Nonlethal Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=5027), [Reach Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=4577), or [Widen Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=4715). The target gains the benefits of the feat on their next turn as though they had taken the [spellshape](/Traits.aspx?ID=513) action themselves; this requires them to [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) as their first action on their turn.

You can’t use this spellshift to affect a creature twice with the same spell. **Success** As critical success, but if the target succeeds at any required saving throw, they are unaffected, and the spell does not change targets.

You’re able to shift yourself into the spaces between to avoid notice. You gain the Part the Veil action.

**Part the Veil** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644)) **Requirements** You are not observed by any enemies; **Effect** You phase yourself into the interstices, veiling yourself from physical reality. You become [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62). You can use this concealment to [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=2404) or [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=2405) as your disassociation from reality makes you difficult to focus on. If you use a [hostile action](/Rules.aspx?ID=2251), this effect ends after the action is complete; otherwise, it lasts for 1 minute.

In the blink of an eye, you transport yourself and any items you’re wearing and holding from your current space to an unoccupied space within 60 feet that you can see. If this would bring another creature with you—even if you’re carrying it in an extradimensional container—you cannot Dart Between. When you arrive at your destination, you can Part the Veil as a free action, even if you wouldn’t normally meet its requirements. If you are [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79), this action does not cause you to become [observed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=84) provided you still have [cover, greater cover,](/Rules.aspx?ID=2372) or [concealment](/Rules.aspx?ID=424) from the creatures you were hidden from after the teleportation.

---

You leave behind an afterimage of yourself in your previous square. This afterimage looks like you and can perform simple behaviors to make the deception more plausible but otherwise cannot move or take actions. A creature can distinguish between you and your afterimage easily. Your afterimage automatically fails all checks and DCs and is destroyed if it would take any damage; otherwise, it lasts for 1 minute. Whenever you take the [Step](/Actions.aspx?ID=2304) action, you can instead teleport to an afterimage instead. If you do, the action gains the [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=710) trait, and the afterimage you teleport to is destroyed.

[World Rouser Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=9376) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 106

**Archetype** [World Rouser](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=396)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)

</column>

---

You know how to wake the world around you from its slumber, whether through your natural affinity for nature or hard-earned knowledge. You gain the Rouse the World action. 

As your ability to converse with the world grows, you can call on it to help you in other ways, some of which require a saving throw. The DC for an ability gained via this archetype is either your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher, and is called your world rouser DC.

**Rouse the World** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) The flora, fauna, and elements in a 10- foot burst within 30 feet stir, aiding you and your allies and whispering in your ear. This area is known as your waking world. While in your waking world, you and your allies gain a +1 circumstance bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) and [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) checks, and you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) checks to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) about creatures and hazards in the area. The effect lasts for 10 minutes, but you can [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311) it. Once per round on subsequent turns, you can [Sustain](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317) this ability to increase the burst’s size by 10 feet. You can Rouse the World in only one area at a time; if you use this ability again, the first area returns to normal.

<title level="2">World Rouser Dedication leads to...</title>
[A Hush Falls Over the World](/Feats.aspx?ID=9383), [All Returns to Slumber](/Feats.aspx?ID=9379), [Awake With a Roar](/Feats.aspx?ID=9386), [Come in From the Wilderness](/Feats.aspx?ID=9384), [Dust Cloud](/Feats.aspx?ID=9381), [Nature's Embrace](/Feats.aspx?ID=9377), [Sheltering Hand](/Feats.aspx?ID=9380), [The World Devours](/Feats.aspx?ID=9385), [The World Whispers](/Feats.aspx?ID=9378), [Wake and Tremble](/Feats.aspx?ID=9382)
name: World Rouser Dedication

A creature in your waking world attempting to use spell or effect with the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541) or [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697) trait must succeed at a DC 4 [flat check](/Rules.aspx?ID=333); on a failure, the spell or effect is [disrupted](/Rules.aspx?ID=2236). On a success, they are not affected by the auditory or sonic effect, though they still may be affected by other aspects of an ability (for example, a creature hit by a weapon with a [_thundering_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2850) rune would not take sonic damage but would still take the normal damage from the weapon).

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 107 **Archetype** [World Rouser](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=396) **Prerequisites** [World Rouser Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=9376) **Requirements** Your waking world is active. --- The ground in your waking world opens to consume a creature standing on it, which must attempt a Reflex save against your world rouser DC. The creature must be Medium or smaller; if your waking world is a 20-foot [burst](/Rules.aspx?ID=2385), the creature can be Large or smaller, or Huge or smaller if your waking world is a 30-foot burst or larger. If you use this ability while your waking world already has a creature [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) or devoured, that creature is automatically freed. If your waking world ends, any creature affected by this ability is automatically freed. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes 3d6 bludgeoning damage.
**Failure** The creature takes 6d6 bludgeoning damage and is [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) by the earth. The creature can attempt to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) against your world rouser DC.
**Critical Failure** The creature is pulled into the earth, which closes above it. It takes 6d6 bludgeoning damage immediately and is devoured. While devoured, it becomes grabbed and [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1, and takes 6d6 bludgeoning damage at the end of each of its turns, and cannot be targeted by any effect. A creature can attempt to Escape against your world rouser DC; in addition to the normal checks to Escape, it can attempt a [Nature](/Domains.aspx?ID=85) check. If it Escapes, it is returned to the area where it was when grabbed. A creature with a [burrow Speed](/Rules.aspx?ID=2348) can Escape automatically and move up to its burrow Speed as part of that action.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Spellshape" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=513" />
<trait label="Wizard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=166" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 109

</column>

---

You imbue your spells with magical force to knock creatures back. If the next action you use is to [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) that has an area of a [burst](/Rules.aspx?ID=2385), [cone](/Rules.aspx?ID=2386), [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387), or [line](/Rules.aspx?ID=2388); has no duration; and requires creatures to attempt a Reflex or Fortitude save, the spell unleashes a forceful blast that pushes creatures away, in addition to its other effects. Each creature that failed its save against the spell is pushed 5 feet, and those who critically failed are pushed 10 feet. If the spell is a cone, emanation, or a line, you push the creature away from yourself. If the spell is a burst, you push the creature away from the center of the burst.
name: Knockback Spell

>
[Redirect Teleportation](/Feats.aspx?ID=9391) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Teleportation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=156" />
<trait label="Wizard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=166" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 109

**Trigger**
A creature teleports into a space within 60 feet of you.

</column>

---

You’re able to intercept a teleportation effect and change where a creature appears. You expend a prepared spell that has the [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=710) trait. You lose your spell slot as if you had cast the triggering spell. You then attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) the triggering spell. The counteract rank for this effect is equal to the rank of the expended spell. If you succeed on your counteract check, you don’t [disrupt](/Rules.aspx?ID=2236) the spell. Instead, you choose an unoccupied space within 60 feet of you for the creature to teleport into. You can’t choose a space that is obviously harmful (such as into a [_wall of fire_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1748) or [hazardous terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2587)) or would cause the target to fall.
name: Redirect Teleportation

[Shared Focus](/Feats.aspx?ID=9392) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Wizard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=166" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 109

**Prerequisites**
[focus pool](/Rules.aspx?ID=2228)

</column>

---

Your magical expertise allows you to perform a metaphorical sleight of hand to manifest a Focus Point. Choose a willing ally within 30 feet who also has a [focus](/Rules.aspx?ID=285) pool. The target gains 1 temporary Focus Point until the start of your next turn, at which time it’s lost, even if not spent. This temporary Focus Point is separate from the Focus Points in their focus pool, allowing them to have it even if they’re at their pool’s maximum. The creature then becomes temporarily immune to Shared Focus until their next daily preparations.
name: Shared Focus

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Wizard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=166" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 109

</column>

---

Your study of different planes of existence makes you more attuned to teleportation effects. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus when you attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) a [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=710) effect. 

When a teleportation effect occurs within 60 feet of you, you detect the location of the effect as a [precise sense](/Rules.aspx?ID=2406). If the effect is a creature teleporting away from that space, you know the general direction of the location to which it teleported but not the distance. However, you can attempt to [Identify Magic](/Actions.aspx?ID=2365) within an hour of the teleportation to know the location to which the creature teleported within 10 miles on a success or 1 mile on a critical success.
name: Spatial Awareness

All the time you’ve spent discussing esoteric theses and performing spell incantations has made your words magical even when you aren’t casting a full spell. <traits>
<trait label="Automaton" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=398" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 111

**Frequency**
once per hour

</column>

---

You have such complete control of your component atoms that you can momentarily separate them far enough apart for you to pass through solid material. You focus on your physical body and will the parts of it to disassemble momentarily. You Stride. You can pass through creatures and tiny cracks during this movement. You cannot pass through solid walls or magical boundaries such as a [_wall of force_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1749). If you haven’t completely passed through a creature or object by the end of your movement, you take 4d6 bludgeoning damage and are shunted to the nearest spot that you can occupy.

**Enhancement** When you use Bodily Disintegration, you can move through solid walls and delay fully reassembling your body, causing you to become [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) until the start of your next turn.
name: Bodily Disintegration

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Revenge of the Runelords</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #220: Crypt of Runes](/Sources.aspx?ID=284) pg. 84

</column>

---

You've become the champion of the runelords of envy. Their support gives you a heightened awareness of your own failings, but you can call their spirits to your side to protect you from harm. The first time each day you critically fail a skill check or saving throw, you gain 1 Mythic Point. You gain the Aegis of Envy activity.

**Activate—Aegis of Envy** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561));  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Spend 1 Mythic Point. The spirits of eight runelords of envy (Naaft, Tannaris, Ivamura, Jurah, Chalsardra, Esedrea, Zarve, Desamelia, and Phirandi) swirl about you for 1 minute. While at least one of the spirits remains, whenever you take damage, you can use a reaction that has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) trait to gain resistance 10 to that damage, or resistance 20 if the damage was dealt by Xanderghul, the runelord of pride. Each time you use this feat to gain resistance, one of the spirits disappears.

<title level="2">Vengeance Feats</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #220: Crypt of Runes](/Sources.aspx?ID=284) pg. 84

During Chapter 2 of this adventure, the PCs can take on the vengeful mantle of a specific runelord's vengeance and embody that need to avenge the violations Runelord Xanderghul has inflicted upon their legacies by creating risen runelords. These rewards manifest in the form of a bonus feat, chosen from the following. A PC can only select one vengeance feat. If you wish to use these feats in the context of another campaign, a mythic PC should be required to use one of their mythic feat slots granted from their mythic destiny.

**Related Feats**: [Avenger of Gluttony](/Feats.aspx?ID=9412), [Avenger of Greed](/Feats.aspx?ID=9413), [Avenger of Lust](/Feats.aspx?ID=9414), [Avenger of Sloth](/Feats.aspx?ID=9415), [Avenger of Wrath](/Feats.aspx?ID=9416)

You've become the champion of the runelords of gluttony, and their hungry spirits are always near you. Whenever a spell or other magical effect restores Hit Points to you, you can choose to reduce the number of Hit Points you regain by any amount. The first time each day you reduce the Hit Points by an amount  equal to your level, you gain 1 Mythic Point. You gain the Gluttonous Feast activity.

**Activate—Gluttonous Feast** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561));  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Spend 1 Mythic Point. The spirits of four runelords of gluttony (Kaliphesta, Atharend, Aethusa, and Goparlis) briefly appear in spaces within 60 feet of you. Each living creature adjacent to at least one of the spirits takes 4d6 void damage per adjacent spirit, to a maximum of 16d6 void damage if they are adjacent to all four spirits. Each target receives a basic Fortitude save against the damage, against the higher of your class DC or spell DC, but Xanderghul, the Runelord of Pride, treats the result of his saving throw as one degree of success worse.

 You gain temporary Hit Points equal to half the damage a single creature takes from this effect; calculate these temporary Hit Points using the creature that took the most damage. These temporary Hit Points last 1 minute.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Revenge of the Runelords</spoilers>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #220: Crypt of Runes](/Sources.aspx?ID=284) pg. 85

</column>

---

You've become a champion of the runelords of sloth. They spur you toward idleness, and their spirits are slow to come to your aid. Once they arrive, however, their combined might is undeniable. The first time each day you spend 10 minutes resting, you gain 1 Mythic Point. During this time, you don't need to sleep, but you can't perform activities like [Refocus](/Actions.aspx?ID=2621) or [Treat Wounds](/Actions.aspx?ID=2399). You gain the Summon Sloth activity.

**Activate—Summon Sloth** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561));  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Spend 1 Mythic Point. You summon the spirit of one of the seven runelords of sloth (Xirie, Ilthyrius, Azeradni, Zalelet, Krenlith, Ivarinna, or Krune) into an unoccupied space within 30 feet. Allies can move through a space occupied by one of these spirits, but a spirit's space is [greater difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366) for your enemies.

 For the next minute, you can use a two-action activity with the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) trait to summon another runelord spirit in a different space within 30 feet, to a maximum of seven spirits. While you are within 120 feet of Xanderghul, the Runelord of Pride, you can summon an additional spirit as a single action (instead of as a two-action activity). At the end of the each of your turns, each spirit fires arcane energy at a different enemy of your choice within 120 feet of it (or does nothing if no enemy is within range), dealing 2d4+2 force damage. After 1 minute, all spirits disappear.

You are the relentless pursuer of your prey that nobody else can see. You can cast 4th-rank _[invisibility](/Spells.aspx?ID=1577)_ as an occult innate spell once per day. When you cast _invisibility_ this way, you select one foe within line of sight. They can see you as if you weren't [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=83), but they also take a –2 circumstance penalty to their Will saves and Will DC for as long as you are invisible and within their line of sight. <traits>

<trait label="Bugbear" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=744" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Cheliax, Infernal Inheritance](/Sources.aspx?ID=372) pg. 30

**Frequency**
once per round

**Prerequisites**
Master in [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36)

**Requirements**
You have a creature [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90).

</column>

---

You choke a victim so that they can barely speak. The creature you have grabbed or restrained takes bludgeoning damage equal to twice your Strength modifier and it can barely speak until the start of your next turn or until it [Escapes](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296), whichever comes first. While it can barely speak, the target can’t vocalize above a hoarse whisper, and it must succeed at a DC 10 flat check or lose any action that requires speech. For an action requiring speech that is also a [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645) action, like Casting a Spell with the concentrate and manipulate trait, the target just rolls a single DC 10 flat check, rather than an additional DC 5 flat check for being grabbed.

[Know I Approach](/Feats.aspx?ID=9440) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Bugbear" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=744" />
<trait label="Emotion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=590" />
<trait label="Fear" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=598" />
<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=647" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=662" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Cheliax, Infernal Inheritance](/Sources.aspx?ID=372) pg. 31

</column>

---

You can enact a short ritual to haunt prey you’ve singled out. Once per day during your daily preparations, you can take 10 minutes to target a creature whose name you know (and who is within 100 miles). Upon completion of the ritual, the target immediately knows you are seeking them out and must attempt a Will save against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. If you have never met the target, it gains a +4 circumstance bonus to the save.

<column gap="tiny">

**Critical Success** The target knows of your intent, but is otherwise unaffected. The target becomes temporarily immune to this ritual for 1 week.

**Success** The target is wracked by a sense of dread at your approach. The next time the target sees you before your next daily preparations, they become [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 1.

**Failure** As success, but the target becomes frightened 2 when they see you. They also become [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=73) by the impending terror for 10 minutes after you perform this ritual.

**Critical Failure** As failure, but the target is [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) 1 for as long as it is fatigued.

</column>
name: Know I Approach

You coax nearby shadows into the shape of a simple weapon or a simple tool or item, using a tiny piece of your shadow to make it solid; in doing so, you lose 1 Hit Point. You can create only level-0 common, non-consumable weapons, or adventuring gear with no intricate parts, written text, or other complicated components. The item lasts until used for a single activity, until you Sculpt Shadows again, or for 1 minute, whichever comes first. Once the duration expires, the object dissipates, and you regain the lost Hit Point unless the item was broken or destroyed. As the object holds a tiny sliver of your shadow, you can’t recover the lost Hit Point until after the object dissipates.
name: Sculpt Shadows

You must spend 10 minutes just after your daily preparations examining the sky or consulting a star chart or you can’t use this action that day.

---

The ancient Saoc Brethren were the masters of astrology, and while your knowledge may be but a pale shadow of their wisdom, it still comes in handy. You recall the stars’ predictions about your current situation. If your next action requires you to attempt one or more skill checks, roll 1d8. On a result of 6, 7, or 8, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to the first such skill check you attempt. On a 3, 4, or 5, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus. On a 2, you gain nothing. On a 1, you take a –1 circumstance penalty to the skill check.

---

By tapping into your ancestral connection to the Netherworld, your corporeal form transforms into the stuff of shadow. For 1 minute, you become as insubstantial as shadow. You gain the [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=632) trait and resistance 10 to all damage except force, spirit, and damage from Strikes with weapons with the _[ghost touch](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2840)_ property; double this resistance against non-magical damage. However, whenever you are in an area of bright light, you are [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71) 3 and [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58); you can't remove these conditions for as long as you remain in bright light. You can [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311) this ability, returning to your solid form.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Polymorph" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=670" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=676" />

**Frequency**
once per week

</column>

---

Calling up deep primal magic, you and a small chosen few are remade into a flock of small birds. In a ceremony that takes 10 minutes to perform, you and up to 5 willing creatures within 15 feet of you are transformed into Tiny birds whose feathers resemble your own. They remain in this form for 8 hours, but an individual target can use the Sustain action to resume its normal shape or return to its bird form. While in this bird form, a target has a land Speed of 15 feet and a fly Speed of 40 feet; in exploration mode, a target can travel 20 miles per hour. A transformed target can’t Strike, cast spells, or use most manipulate actions.
name: Flock As One

**Source** [Cheliax, Infernal Inheritance](/Sources.aspx?ID=372) pg. 78 **Archetype** [Hellbound Aspirant](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=397) **Prerequisites** You do not have the [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) trait. --- You’ve acquired a taste of infernal power at a very high price: When you die, your soul belongs to Hell. When you take this dedication, you are branded by your benefactor’s influence with a permanent mark. The mark usually appears on your hand and can be [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) by mundane or magical means.

You gain resistance to fire equal to half your level and the Invoke Infernal Bargain action.
**Invoke Infernal Bargain** **Requirements** You are not [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67); **Effect** You call upon your infernal pact to surge with devilish power. You gain a +2 status bonus to the next attack roll, skill check, or saving throw you attempt before the end of your next turn. You then become doomed 1. **Special** You can’t retrain out of this feat unless you are able to terminate the agreement that gives you power, usually a contract with a devil. This requires a [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) check against a very hard DC of your level, though the GM might set a higher DC depending on how many feats you’ve taken from this dedication. On a failure, you can’t attempt to retrain out of this feat for 1 year. On a critical failure, a clause in your contract invokes an additional penalty, usually causing you to become doomed 1 for the next year, although the GM might determine a more appropriate punishment. Hellbound Aspirant Dedication leads to... [Call Hellfire](/Feats.aspx?ID=9483), [Devil In Disguise](/Feats.aspx?ID=9481), [Devil's Wings](/Feats.aspx?ID=9487), [Dispute Terms](/Feats.aspx?ID=9485), [Fiendish Arms](/Feats.aspx?ID=9479), [Infernal Anguish](/Feats.aspx?ID=9484), [Infernal Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=9482), [The Devil Inside](/Feats.aspx?ID=9486), [Unholy Pact](/Feats.aspx?ID=9480)
name: Hellbound Aspirant Dedication

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Legal Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) or Trained in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)

**Access**
You’re from Isger.

</column>

---

Your studies allow you to wield the magic locked within infernal contracts without surrendering your soul. You gain a contract folio with four common divine cantrips of your choice, which functions as a spellbook; this folio may be a collection of contracts you have already studied or the charred remains of one you were once bound to. You gain the Cast a Spell activity. You can prepare two cantrips each day from your folio. You’re trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. Your key spellcasting attribute for infernal pactbreaker spells is Intelligence, and they are divine infernal pactbreaker spells. You can always use Legal Lore or Religion to Decipher the Writing of a contract, and if you roll a critical failure on such a check, you get a failure instead.

<title level="2">Infernal Pactbreaker Dedication leads to...</title>
[Annul Compulsion](/Feats.aspx?ID=9492), [Basic Pactbreaker Spellcasting](/Feats.aspx?ID=9489), [Clarify Hellfire](/Feats.aspx?ID=9496), [Commandeer Hellmouth](/Feats.aspx?ID=9500), [Condemn Soul](/Feats.aspx?ID=9494), [Contract Blade](/Feats.aspx?ID=9490), [Diabolic Usurpation](/Feats.aspx?ID=9491), [Impose Order (Pactbreaker)](/Feats.aspx?ID=9493), [Proscribe Devilry](/Feats.aspx?ID=9497)

Turning the diabolic powers of a contract inward, you cause the paper to fold and sharpen into a deadly blade. When you Interact to draw your contract folio, you can use a free action with the [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645) trait to transform it into a weapon. A contract blade deals 1d6 slashing damage, is a simple weapon in the [sword group](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=15), and has the [finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=602), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), and [parry](/Traits.aspx?ID=667) traits. If the blade leaves your hands, it returns to its original form. You can buy and inscribe fundamental weapon runes and weapon property runes into your folio in the same way you would for a regular weapon, and they apply to your contract blade. You can move runes to and from your folio to other weapons or runestones for the usual cost.

You know how to siphon the power hellish deities give devils without offering up worship. You gain the cleric's [Domain Initiate](/Feats.aspx?ID=4644) feat but must select [fire](/Domains.aspx?ID=76), [trickery](/Domains.aspx?ID=94), or [tyranny](/Domains.aspx?ID=96) as your domain. Many of the traps in the terms of a diabolic contract rely on curses, charms, or enchantments that enforce the behavior of the signatory. You've learned to draft amendments which nullify such effects, allowing others to walk free. You attempt to counteract a curse, a spell that alters how someone behaves such as _[charm](/Spells.aspx?ID=1463)_, or the [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63), [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=64) or [fascinated](/Conditions.aspx?ID=72) conditions. Regardless of the outcome, the target is then temporarily immune to your Annul Compulsion for 1 day.

With a quick flourish, you draw together runes and legal bindings to condemn a creature’s soul and bring it to justice. Select a creature within 30 feet of you; that creature must attempt a Will save against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. Regardless of the result, the target is then temporarily immune to your Condemn Soul for 1 day.

<column gap="tiny">

**Success** The target is unaffected.

**Failure** Your condemnation frays the fabric of the target’s soul. The target gains weakness to fire and spirit damage equal to half your level for 1 minute. Only you can trigger this weakness.

**Critical Failure** As failure, but any creature can trigger the creature’s weakness.

</column>

You can manipulate the size, shape and movements of your shadow as you desire, though it can't stretch beyond twice its normal size. In addition, you can use your shadow to increase your reach to 10 feet when delivering spells with a range of touch.

You also have access to the [School of Shadow Veils](/ArcaneSchools.aspx?ID=36). These spells share the tradition, spell attack modifier, and spell DC of the spells you used to meet this archetype's prerequisites, as do any focus spells granted by midnight illusionist feats. You have dedicated yourself to guiding others to liberty and safety. You gain a +5-foot status bonus to your Speed. Choose up to six other people to be your “crop.” You can add or remove someone from your crop by spending 10 minutes in conversation with them. The creature is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) to your Strike, but the bomb doesn’t deal its [splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=699) damage.

You can adulterate alchemical mutagens with volatile goblin oils that spill from your pores, coating your weapons and skin. <column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Cheliax, Infernal Inheritance](/Sources.aspx?ID=372) pg. 199

**Prerequisites**
[bomber research field](/ResearchFields.aspx?ID=5)

</column>

---

You can mix slow-burning fuels into your alchemical bombs that deal [persistent damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86), making their effects linger. When you Strike with the bomb, it deals no damage on a direct hit (though it still deals [splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=699) damage and applies other effects such as saving throws); you can also Strike an empty space with the bomb, automatically succeeding on your attack roll. On a failure, success, or critical success, the bomb’s contents spread in the target’s space, creating a lingering alchemical flame. The first time a creature enters the flame on its turn or starts its turn in the flame, it takes damage of the same amount and type as the bomb’s persistent damage. The flame lasts for 1 minute or until an adjacent creature uses an Interact action to smother it.
name: Lingering Bomb

You become an expert in Performance. If you were already an expert, you instead become trained in your choice of Nature or Fey Lore. You also gain the Stellar Dance Stance action.

**Stellar Dance Stance** ([primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676), [stance](/Traits.aspx?ID=701)) **Requirements** You aren't [encumbered](/Conditions.aspx?ID=70) or wearing medium or heavy armor; **Effect** You dance as freely as the stars above. While in this stance, you can attempt a Performance check instead of an [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) check to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) or [Tumble Through](/Actions.aspx?ID=2370). When you succeed at such a check, your stance reaches its zenith. While your dance is at its zenith, your Strikes with agile or finesse weapons and unarmed attacks deal additional force damage equal to the number of weapon damage dice.

Your stance stays at its zenith until the start of your next turn or until you leave the stance, whichever comes first, and you can't bring your stance to its zenith if it's already at its zenith. If you gain more ways to reach the zenith through other feats, these restrictions apply to those methods, too. Stellar Dancer Dedication leads to... Just as the celestial bodies of the sun and moon align in perfect synchronicity, so too can you perform two steps of the stellar dance at once. You take any action you have from the stellar dancer archetype that requires your dance to not be at its zenith, ignoring that requirement. If that action would cause your dance to reach its zenith, your dance remains at its zenith until the end of your next turn or until you leave the stance, whichever comes first.

You've created or been given one of the weapons of living wood or crystal wielded by the wild hunt. Your living weapon can be any common simple or martial weapon, or any other simple or martial weapon to which you have access, except it must be made of wood or crystal and gains the [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676) trait. Your living weapon has the effects of a _[shifting](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2846)_ rune, except that it can also take the shape of a ranged weapon or an innocuous form, such as a walking stick, when activated. This rune doesn't count toward the weapon's maximum number of property runes. If your living weapon is destroyed, you can regrow it in your hands during your next daily preparations; the replacement retains any runes the weapon had before it was destroyed.
name: Living Weapon

[Pitiless Pursuit](/Feats.aspx?ID=9554) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=695" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Feybound](/Sources.aspx?ID=379) pg. 30

**Archetype** [Wild Hunter](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=403)

**Prerequisites**
[Wild Hunter Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=9552); Expert in [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49); Master in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)

</column>

---

Fey magic duplicates your footsteps or the hoofbeats of your mount, filling the wilderness around your quarry and running them ragged until they’re softened for the kill. When you [Track](/Actions.aspx?ID=2408) a single creature, you can also attempt a Nature check against a standard DC for your quarry’s level. If you do, Track gains the [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=629) and [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676) traits.

<column gap="tiny">

**Critical Success** The creature becomes [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 1 and [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=73) for as long as it’s frightened, and it can’t reduce its frightened value below 1 until you stop Tracking it. If you enter an encounter that includes the creature while Tracking it, it can’t reduce its frightened condition until after you’ve taken your first turn.

**Success** As critical success, but the creature isn’t fatigued for as long as it’s frightened.

**Critical Failure** You become fatigued until your next daily preparations or until the end of your first turn in an encounter that includes the creature, whichever comes first.

</column>

<title level="2">Pitiless Pursuit leads to...</title>
[Pursuing Doom](/Feats.aspx?ID=9558)

**Source** [Feybound](/Sources.aspx?ID=379) pg. 30 **Archetype** [Wild Hunter](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=403) **Prerequisites** [Wild Hunter Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=9552); trained in light or medium armor --- The hides and bones of mighty beasts and the leaves and bark of the old-cold forest become your second skin, concealing your body and leaving it unhindered to better partake in the wild hunt. You gain the armor specialization effects for light and medium armor from the [leather](/ArmorGroups.aspx?ID=3), [skeletal](/ArmorGroups.aspx?ID=6), and [wood](/ArmorGroups.aspx?ID=7) armor groups. You don't become [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=73) if you sleep while wearing such armor.

In addition, while you wear such armor, you can [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=2388) creatures with the [animal](/Traits.aspx?ID=531), [beast](/Traits.aspx?ID=547), [fey](/Traits.aspx?ID=599), or [plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=668) traits, so long as they're either the same size as you or one size larger. Impersonate gains the [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=629) and [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676) traits when used this way. Impersonating a larger creature doesn't change your size.
name: Skins Of The Slain
prerequisite: Wild Hunter Dedication; trained in light or medium armor

You entwine your arrows and spears with fey magic that signals the opening of the hunt. You can Interact to draw a ranged weapon or a weapon with the thrown trait, then you make a ranged Strike against a creature you were tracking. If your hunting partner is in your wild link aura, the target is also off-guard to your hunting partner’s first attack against it before the end of their first turn.

Your jokes can get a whole battlefield laughing. A creature within 30 feet must attempt a Will save against your [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) DC.

<column gap="tiny">

**Critical Success** The target is unaffected, and Infectious Joke ends for all targets.

**Success** The target is plagued with uncontrollable laughter. It can’t use reactions for the duration of the effect. **Failure** As success, but the target is also [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1.

**Critical Failure** As failure, but the target also falls [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88).

</column>

You permanently alter the terrain of an area. You can spend 1 day of downtime to turn an open, unoccupied area of land within a 15-foot emanation into a copse of trees, a small pond, or a rocky hill as long as you have an affinity for that type of terrain. For each additional day of downtime you spend, you can expand the emanation by an additional 10 feet (to a maximum of a 100-foot emanation). If left undisturbed, the altered terrain will naturally attract wild animals and adapt to the surrounding terrain with each year that passes.

<traits>
